definition_zh: 社会行为；同种个体彼此影响、彼此回应的行为
definition_en: the behavior by which members of the same species act on one another and respond to one another
core_image: 两只动物面对面交换信号，一个动作引来另一个动作
scene: 午后草地上，两只幼犬互相追逐，轮流咬住对方的颈毛又松开。 The two puppies chase and mouth each other in turn, and ethologists treat this exchange as social behavior.
sceneCN: 这里 social behavior 指「同种个体之间彼此作用的行为」（第 1 个义项：一方的动作引起另一方的回应）；句意为两只幼犬轮流追逐、轻咬，行为学家把这种一来一往视为社会行为。图中可辨识物件：草地、两只幼犬、扬起的尾巴、来回的奔跑路线。

pos.zh: 社会行为（同种个体之间的相互作用；作不可数名词，指具体类型时可有复数）

senses.title: Interaction between members of one species
senses.titleCN: 同种个体之间的相互作用
senses.definition: actions directed at other members of the same species that invite or provoke a response
senses.definitionCN: 指向同种其他个体、并引起对方回应的动作
senses.example: The two puppies chase and mouth each other in turn.
senses.exampleCN: 两只幼犬轮流追逐、轻咬对方。
senses.why: social names the partner, and behavior names the act; together the phrase marks any act whose meaning depends on another individual's response.
senses.whyCN: social 指明对象是同伴，behavior 指明动作；合起来标记的是「意义取决于对方回应」的动作。

senses.title: Cooperation and mutual aid
senses.definition: behavior in which individuals work together and share the benefit
senses.definitionCN: 个体共同做事并分享好处的行为
senses.example: The pair takes turns incubating the eggs so both can feed.
senses.exampleCN: 这一对鸟轮流孵卵，使双方都能外出觅食。
senses.why: living in a group forces cooperation: one animal's action must fit another's, and the fit itself becomes a recognizable pattern.
senses.whyCN: 群居迫使个体合作：一只动物的动作必须与另一只配合，而这种配合本身成为可辨认的模式。

senses.title: Affiliative behavior: bonding and play
senses.titleCN: 亲近行为：结盟、梳理与玩耍
senses.definition: behavior that builds and maintains friendly bonds, such as grooming, play and contact
senses.definitionCN: 建立并维持友好关系的动作，如梳理、玩耍与身体接触
senses.example: Young monkeys groom one another for hours after a quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 小猴子争吵之后会互相梳理毛发好几个小时。
senses.why: a group needs more than cooperation; it needs glue, and grooming and play are the visible glue.
senses.whyCN: 群体不只需要合作，还需要黏合剂；梳理与玩耍就是看得见的黏合剂。

senses.title: Agonistic behavior: rivalry and rank
senses.definition: behavior used in contests over resources, mates or rank, including threat and submission
senses.definitionCN: 为资源、配偶或等级而竞争的行为，包括威胁与退让
senses.example: Two stags lower their antlers before either charges.
senses.exampleCN: 两只雄鹿在冲撞之前先低下头角。
senses.why: the same social channel carries conflict; a threat is still an act aimed at another animal and still waits for its answer.
senses.whyCN: 同一条社会通道也承载冲突；威胁仍然是针对另一只动物的动作，仍然等待对方回答。

senses.title: Communication through signals
senses.definition: the exchange of calls, displays or scents that carries information between individuals
senses.definitionCN: 个体之间传递信息的叫声、展示或气味交换
senses.example: A sentinel bird calls and the flock moves into cover.
senses.exampleCN: 一只警戒鸟发出叫声，鸟群随即躲进遮蔽处。
senses.why: interaction requires a channel; communication is the part of social behavior that carries the message rather than the action itself.
senses.whyCN: 相互作用需要通道；交流是社会行为中传递信息的部分，而非动作本身。

senses.title: Group living and division of labour
senses.definition: the organized behavior of a group, including coordinated movement, sentinels and division of labour
senses.definitionCN: 群体的组织化行为，包括协同移动、警戒与劳动分工
senses.example: The colony sends foragers out while others guard the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 蚁群派觅食者外出，另一些则守卫入口。
senses.why: when many individuals act as one unit, the unit itself has behavior; the phrase scales from two animals to a colony.
senses.whyCN: 当许多个体像一个单位那样行动时，这个单位本身就有行为；短语因此可从两只动物扩大到整个群体。

senses.title: Human social conduct
senses.titleCN: 人际关系中的举止与规范
senses.definition: the way people act toward others, including politeness, cooperation and social norms
senses.definitionCN: 人对待他人的方式，包括礼貌、合作与社会规范
senses.example: Guests greet the host before finding a seat.
senses.exampleCN: 客人先向主人问好，再找位置坐下。
senses.why: people also respond to one another under learned rules, so the term crosses from ethology into sociology without changing its shape.
senses.whyCN: 人也在习得规则之下彼此回应，因此这个术语从动物行为学进入社会学时并未改变形状。

senses.title: A research category
senses.titleCN: 行为研究中的可观察类别
senses.definition: a class of observable actions recorded in studies of groups, from grooming bouts to chase sequences
senses.definitionCN: 群体研究中记录的一类可观察动作，从梳理时段到追逐序列
senses.example: The observer scores every grooming bout as social behavior.
senses.exampleCN: 观察者把每个梳理时段记为社会行为。
senses.why: to compare species or groups, the researcher must cut the stream of action into named units, and this phrase is one such unit.
senses.whyCN: 要比较物种或群体，研究者必须把连续的动作切成有名字的单位，而这个短语就是这样一个单位。

intro.en: Social comes from Latin socius 'companion' through socialis, while behavior is a native English formation from be- plus have. The phrase is used in both ethology and sociology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: social 经 socialis 源自拉丁 socius「同伴」；behavior 是英语本土构造，由 be- 加 have 构成。这个短语同时用于动物行为学与社会学。年代为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, associate, ally'; it named a person one travelled or acted with, not a crowd in general.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、伙伴、盟友」，指与自己同行或共同行动的人，而不是泛指人群。

items.en: Socialis 'of companions, allied' was formed from socius and gave English social through Old French.
items.cn: socialis 意为「同伴的、结盟的」，由 socius 构成，经古法语进入英语成为 social。

items.era: OLD ENGLISH AND MIDDLE ENGLISH BEHAVE
items.en: Behavior derives from behave, Middle English be- plus have (Old English habban 'to hold'); the noun first meant a manner of bearing oneself.
items.cn: behavior 来自 behave，即中古英语 be- 加 have（古英语 habban「持有」）；名词最初指持守自己的方式。

items.en: Social behavior became a shared term in sociology and in animal behavior studies in the twentieth century, where it covers everything from grooming to group defence.
items.cn: 20 世纪，social behavior 成为社会学与动物行为学的共用术语，涵盖从梳理到群体防卫的各种动作。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest use of the compound in either discipline is not precisely dated, and the line between social and merely gregarious behavior is drawn differently by different authors.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这一复合词在两个学科中的最早用法都没有精确年代；不同作者对「社会行为」与「仅仅群聚」的界线划分不一。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same social stem; group two holds neighboring concepts that are often used as if they were synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 social 词干构成的词；第二组是常被当作同义词使用的邻近概念。

entries.definition: Relating to society or companionship; it describes the setting, while social behavior names what is actually done.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「社会的、社交的」；描述场景，而 social behavior 才指实际做出的动作。

entries.definition: Fond of company and easy in conversation; it describes a temperament, not a recorded pattern of action.
entries.definitionCN: 喜欢与人相处、谈吐自在；描述性情，而非被记录的动作模式。

entries.definition: The degree to which a species lives in groups; it is a property of a species, not a single observable act.
entries.definitionCN: 一个物种群居的程度；是物种的属性，而非单个可观察的动作。

entries.definition: Relating to society as a whole, as in societal change; it does not describe individual interaction.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「整个社会的」，如社会变迁；不描述个体之间的互动。

entries.definition: A single episode of mutual action; social behavior is the broader class of such episodes and their patterns.
entries.definitionCN: 一次相互作用的片段；social behavior 是这类片段及其模式的更大类别。

entries.definition: The transfer of information by signals; it is one component of social behavior, not its whole span.
entries.definitionCN: 通过信号传递信息；是社会行为的一个组成部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: The behavior of a whole group as a unit; social behavior can also describe two individuals.
entries.definitionCN: 整个群体作为一个单位的行为；social behavior 也可以只描述两个个体。

entries.definition: Action carried out alone, without response from others; it is the contrast case that defines the social one.
entries.definitionCN: 独自完成、没有他人回应的动作；它是对照项，用来界定社会行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: socius 'companion' gives socialis and social; social behavior is literally the behavior of companions.
normal.cn: socius「同伴」构成 socialis 与 social；social behavior 字面上就是「同伴之间的行为」。

normal.en: The family runs social, sociable, sociality, socialize and societal.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 social、sociable、sociality、socialize 与 societal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: grooming, play, threat, sentinel call, division of labour.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：梳理、玩耍、威胁、警戒叫声、劳动分工。

normal.en: Ask two questions: is another individual involved, and does the act depend on that individual's response?
normal.cn: 问两个问题：是否涉及另一个个体？这个动作是否取决于对方的回应？

normal.en: Social behavior is studied at two scales: the pair and the group.
normal.cn: 社会行为在两个尺度上研究：一对个体与整个群体。

abstract.en: Picture two dancers who must each read the other's weight before moving.
abstract.cn: 想象两个舞者，每次移动前都要读懂对方的重心。

abstract.en: Picture a flock turning as one body because each bird watches its neighbour.
abstract.cn: 想象鸟群像一个身体那样转向，因为每只鸟都在看邻居。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every greeting is an answer to the greeting before it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，每声问候都是对前一声问候的回答。

examples.en: Grooming is the most reliable measure of social behavior in many primates.
examples.cn: 梳理在许多灵长类中是衡量社会行为最可靠的指标。

examples.en: Play teaches young animals the rules they will need in a group.
examples.cn: 玩耍让幼兽学会群体中将要用到的规则。

examples.en: A sentinel's call changes the whole flock's behavior within seconds.
examples.cn: 警戒鸟的一声叫能在几秒内改变整群鸟的行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: social（同伴的）+ behavior（行为）——同伴之间你来我往的动作 → 社会行为

root: social 源自拉丁 socius「同伴」，经 socialis 进入英语；behavior 源自中古英语 behaven，由 be- 加古英语 habban「持有」构成。合指「同伴之间相互作用的行为」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move outward from one exchange: two individuals respond, then cooperate, bond, compete, signal, form a group, follow human rules, and finally become a unit in a researcher's notebook.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一次交换向外扩展：两个个体回应、合作、结盟、竞争、传信号、组成群体、遵循人的规范，最后成为研究者笔记里的一个单位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: action aimed at another, answered by that other, so the loop closes.
core.cn: 核心意象：指向另一个个体的动作，被对方回应，于是闭环成立。

branches.en: THE LOOP: a social act is defined by the reply it expects.
branches.cn: 闭环：社会动作由它所期待的回应来定义。

branches.en: GLUE: cooperation and grooming hold the pair together in two different ways.
branches.cn: 黏合：合作与梳理以两种不同方式把一对个体维系在一起。

branches.en: TENSION AND SIGNAL: rivalry and communication are the same channel under different loads.
branches.cn: 张力与信号：竞争与交流是同一条通道在不同负荷下的状态。

branches.en: SCALE: when the loop repeats many times, a group acquires behavior of its own.
branches.cn: 尺度：当闭环多次重复，群体便获得属于自己的行为。

branches.en: TWO READINGS: the same acts can be judged as conduct or counted as data.
branches.cn: 两种读法：同样的动作既可被评判为举止，也可被计为数据。

intro.en: Social behavior joins a Latin companionship word to an English manner-word; the social half carries the borrowed family, the behavior half the native one.
intro.cn: social behavior 把一个拉丁「同伴」词与一个英语「方式」词连起来；social 一半承载借词族，behavior 一半承载本族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius 'companion' yields socialis and societas; English draws social, sociable, sociality and societal from that line. Behavior is Germanic and has no Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius「同伴」衍生 socialis 与 societas；英语由此得到 social、sociable、sociality 与 societal。behavior 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。

items.example: Socius named the person one acted with.
items.exampleCN: socius 指与自己共同行动的人。

items.example: Socialis is the direct source of English social.
items.exampleCN: socialis 是英语 social 的直接来源。

items.example: Societas survives in the word society.
items.exampleCN: societas 留在 society 一词中。

items.example: Social insects live in organized groups.
items.exampleCN: 社会性昆虫生活在有组织的群体中。

items.meaning: the quality of living in groups
items.exampleCN: 哺乳动物的社会性差异很大。

items.example: Behavior is the observable side of social life.
items.exampleCN: 行为是社会生活中可观察的一面。

items.meaning: about, around; makes a verb transitive
items.exampleCN: be- 加 have 构成 behave。
行为研究会计数梳理时段。
合群的动物会主动寻找同伴。

definition_zh: 由……伴随；伴有；附有（强调两件事同时出现或一并到来）
definition_en: to happen or appear together with something else, or to have something added alongside
core_image: 山谷地震过后，坡面滑下一片土石，轰鸣声与扬起的尘土同时出现
scene: 山区地震过后，救援队看到坡面上滑下一片土石，山脚的公路被埋了半截。 Ground shaking in steep valleys can be accompanied by landslides that block the roads below.
sceneCN: 这里指地面震动与山体滑坡同时出现（第 1 个义项：两个事件同时发生）；句意为陡峭山谷中的地面震动可能伴有阻断下方公路的滑坡。图中可辨识物件：裂开的山坡、滑落的土石、被埋的公路、扬起的尘土。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）由……伴随；伴有；附有

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心动词，义为「陪伴、伴随」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「伴随物、伴奏」
与本词同出「分面包的人」一语，义为「同伴」
同出「同伴」一语，义为「陪伴、公司」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「无人陪伴的」

senses.title: Happening at the same time
senses.definition: to occur together with another event, without one causing the other
senses.definitionCN: 指与另一事件一起出现，但不暗示其中一个导致另一个
senses.example: The first storm can be accompanied by a sharp fall in air pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 第一场风暴可能伴有气压骤降。
senses.why: The passive frame puts the main event first and the companion second, which is why by marks the follower.
senses.whyCN: 被动框架把主事件放前、伴随者放后，所以 by 标出的是跟着来的那一方。

senses.title: A symptom alongside an illness
senses.definition: to appear as an additional sign of a medical condition
senses.definitionCN: 指作为某种疾病的附加体征出现
senses.example: The fever can be accompanied by a dry cough and a loss of appetite.
senses.exampleCN: 发热可能伴有干咳与食欲下降。
senses.why: Medicine separates the main sign from its companions, and the phrase keeps the two in one report.
senses.whyCN: 医学把主征与伴随征分开，而这个词把两者留在同一份报告里。

senses.title: Music playing alongside
senses.definition: to have music or sound performed together with the main part
senses.definitionCN: 指与主要部分一同演奏的音乐或声音
senses.example: The solo can be accompanied by a single piano throughout the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 这个独奏在第二乐章里可能全程由一架钢琴伴奏。
senses.why: The oldest musical sense keeps the picture of one voice walking beside another.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的音乐义仍保留着「一个声部走在另一个声部旁边」的画面。

senses.title: A document sent together
senses.definition: to be sent or presented together with another document
senses.definitionCN: 指与另一份文件一起送交或呈上
senses.example: The application can be accompanied by two letters of recommendation.
senses.exampleCN: 申请材料可能附有两封推荐信。
senses.why: The companion here is paper, and the phrase turns physical attachment into an official relation.
senses.whyCN: 这里的伴随者是纸张，这个短语把物理上的「附在一起」变成一种正式的关联。

senses.title: A condition attached
senses.definition: to come with a stated condition or requirement
senses.definitionCN: 指同时带有某项说明的条件或要求
senses.example: The permit can be accompanied by a condition that limits work to daylight hours.
senses.exampleCN: 许可证可能附有一项把施工限制在白天的条件。
senses.why: Attachment becomes obligation: what comes along can also bind the person who receives it.
senses.whyCN: 「附在一起」变成义务：跟着来的东西也会约束收下它的人。

senses.title: A linked natural event
senses.definition: to have a secondary natural event follow the main one closely
senses.definitionCN: 指紧跟着主要事件出现次一级的自然现象
senses.example: A large earthquake can be accompanied by aftershocks for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 大地震可能在数周内伴有余震。
senses.why: Nature supplies the clearest pairs, which is why the phrase is so common in geology.
senses.whyCN: 自然提供了最清楚的成对现象，所以这个短语在地质学里格外常见。

senses.title: A person going along
senses.definition: to have someone travel or attend together with the subject
senses.definitionCN: 指有人与主语一同前往或出席
senses.example: A minor can be accompanied by a parent at the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 未成年人面谈时可以由父母陪同。
senses.why: The oldest sense is human: one person walks beside another, and the grammar keeps that picture.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是关于人的：一个人走在另一个人身旁，语法把这一画面保留下来。

senses.title: A cost that comes along
senses.definition: to bring an unwelcome consequence along with a benefit
senses.definitionCN: 指在带来好处的同时附带不受欢迎的后果
senses.example: Rapid growth can be accompanied by rising inequality in the same region.
senses.exampleCN: 快速增长可能伴有同一地区不平等加剧。
senses.why: The companion can be a burden, and the phrase does not promise that what follows is welcome.
senses.whyCN: 伴随者也可能是负担，这个短语并不保证跟来的是好事。

intro.en: Accompany reached English through Old French accompagner, from a and compaign, companion, and that noun goes back to Late Latin companio, com- plus panis, bread, literally one who shares bread. The passive frame be accompanied by is a later English construction; its first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: accompany 经古法语 accompagner 进入英语，来自 a 与 compaign「同伴」，而后者上溯晚期拉丁语 companio，由 com-「共同」与 panis「面包」构成，字面是「分面包的人」。被动框架「be accompanied by」是更晚的英语构造，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Panis meant bread, the food that made shared meals a picture of trust.
items.cn: panis 意为面包，是让共餐成为信任画面的那种食物。

items.en: Com- plus panis named one who shares bread, and so a companion.
items.cn: com- 与 panis 合成「分面包的人」，也就是同伴。

items.en: The French verb meant to keep someone company, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 这个法语动词意为与某人作伴，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: Early English used accompany for people travelling together before it extended to things.
items.cn: 早期英语用 accompany 指人一同出行，之后才扩展到事物。

items.en: By marks the companion in the passive, a native English pattern rather than part of the borrowed word; its first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 被动句里由 by 标出伴随者，这是英语本土框架而非借词的一部分，首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the bread root or the same verb; the second group names neighbouring ideas of going together and following.
note.cn: 第一组共享「面包」词根或同一动词；第二组是与「同行、随后」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The active verb meaning to go with or add to something.
entries.definitionCN: 指同去或附加的主动动词。

entries.definition: Something that goes along with another, especially music.
entries.definitionCN: 指随另一物而来的东西，尤指伴奏。

entries.definition: A person who shares a journey or a meal.
entries.definitionCN: 指同路或共餐的人。

entries.definition: The state of being together, and later a business.
entries.definitionCN: 指同在的状态，后来也指公司。

entries.definition: Without anyone or anything going along.
entries.definitionCN: 指无人或无所伴随。

entries.definition: To have something come after in time, which stresses order rather than company.
entries.definitionCN: 指时间上随后发生，强调先后而非同时。

entries.definition: To happen at the same time, often by chance.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时发生，常含偶然之意。

entries.definition: To be included along with something.
entries.definitionCN: 指与某物一并包括在内。

entries.definition: To accompany or agree with something.
entries.definitionCN: 指伴随或赞同某事。

entries.definition: To be joined with something as a pair.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为一对与某物结合。

entries.definition: To be present with or to go with, in formal usage.
entries.definitionCN: 指伴随或出席，属正式用法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations keep the bread picture, the simultaneous sense of by, and the contrast with words that only mark sequence.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想保留「面包」的画面、介词的「同时」义，并把它与只标先后的词作对照。

normal.en: Com plus panis is 'with bread', so a companion is someone you share bread with.
normal.cn: com 加 panis 是「带面包」，所以同伴就是与你分面包的人。

normal.en: By marks the companion, not the cause; the storm is not caused by the landslide.
normal.cn: by 标出的是伴随者而非原因；风暴不是滑坡造成的。

normal.en: Accompanied by is simultaneous, followed by is sequential, and the two are not interchangeable.
normal.cn: accompanied by 是同时，followed by 是先后，两者不能互换。

normal.en: Documents are accompanied by letters, patients by symptoms, children by adults.
normal.cn: 文件附信，病人带症状，孩子由大人陪同。

normal.en: The companion can be unpleasant, as when growth is accompanied by inequality.
normal.cn: 伴随者也可以是不快的，比如增长伴有不平等。

abstract.en: Every main event casts a shadow of smaller events, and the phrase names that shadow.
abstract.cn: 每个主事件都会投下较小事件的影子，这个短语就给影子命名。

abstract.en: Sharing bread is the oldest form of agreement, and the grammar still remembers it.
abstract.cn: 分面包是最古老的约定形式，语法至今还记得它。

abstract.en: What comes along is not always a gift; sometimes it is the bill.
abstract.cn: 跟来的不总是礼物，有时是账单。

examples.en: The announcement can be accompanied by a short written summary.
examples.cn: 这项公告可能附有一份简短的书面摘要。

examples.en: Heavy rain can be accompanied by strong winds along the coast.
examples.cn: 沿海的大雨可能伴有强风。

examples.en: The treatment can be accompanied by mild fatigue for a few days.
examples.cn: 这种治疗可能伴有数日的轻度疲劳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 阿康泊尼德 拜」——分面包的人跟着来：由……伴随

root: 古法语 accompagner，源于晚期拉丁语 companio「同伴」，由 com-「共同」与 panis「面包」构成，本义「分面包的人」；英语十四世纪借入。被动框架属后起英语构造。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a second thing arriving with the first: an event, a symptom, music, a document, a condition, a natural sequel, a person and a cost.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述第二件事与第一件同时到来：事件、症状、音乐、文件、条件、自然连带、同行的人与代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the ground shakes and the slope slides in the same minute.
core.cn: 核心意象：地面震动与山坡滑落发生在同一分钟里。

branches.en: THE PAIR: two events share one stretch of time.
branches.cn: 成对：两个事件共用同一段时间。

branches.en: THE BODY: a main sign brings a second sign with it.
branches.cn: 身体：主征把次征一起带来。

branches.en: THE SOUND AND THE PAPER: music plays beside the solo, and a letter travels with a form.
branches.cn: 声音与纸张：音乐在独奏旁响起，信件随表格同行。

branches.en: THE TERMS AND THE EARTH: a permit carries a condition, and a quake carries aftershocks.
branches.cn: 条件与大地：许可带着条件，地震带着余震。

branches.en: THE WALKER AND THE BILL: a person walks beside another, and growth brings its cost.
branches.cn: 同行者与账单：有人走在旁边，增长带来代价。

intro.en: The family is built on a Latin word for bread, with prefixes marking togetherness and endings marking roles.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语「面包」一词上，前缀标出「共同」，词尾标出角色。

latinIntro.en: Latin panis and Late Latin companio supply the core; com- and -ment, -ion, -y build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 panis 与晚期拉丁语 companio 提供核心，com- 与 -ment、-ion、-y 构成其余部分。

items.example: It supplies the second half of companion.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 companion 的后一半。

items.example: It marks the sharing of the bread.
items.exampleCN: 它标出面包是共同分食的。

items.example: It is the source of companion and company.
items.exampleCN: 它是 companion 与 company 的来源。

items.example: It carried the word into English.
It forms companion from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由同一词干构成 companion。

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心动词，义为「陪伴、伴随」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「伴随物、伴奏」
同出「分面包的人」一语，义为「同伴」
同出「同伴」一语，义为「陪伴、公司」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「无人陪伴的」

definition_zh: 使石化；使吓呆；使僵化
definition_en: to turn into stone, or to make a person or an institution unable to move
core_image: 一滴含矿物的水长年滴在木头上，木头慢慢变成了石头
scene: 他站在门口，看见母亲的脸色，整个人像被浇成了石头。 He stood in the doorway, saw his mother's face, and felt the news petrify him where he stood.
sceneCN: 这里 petrify 指吓得整个人僵住（第 3 个义项：使吓呆）；句意为他在门口看见母亲的脸色，那条消息把他吓得当场僵住。

pos.zh: 使石化；使吓呆；使僵化

senses.title: Turn to stone
senses.definition: to change organic matter into stone over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 在漫长岁月里把有机物变成石头
senses.example: The wood had petrified under layers of ash.
senses.exampleCN: 那木头在层层火山灰下已经石化。
senses.why: This is the mineral sense, slow and geological.
senses.whyCN: 这是矿物义，缓慢而地质性。

senses.title: Fossilize
senses.definition: to preserve a living shape by replacing its substance with stone
senses.definitionCN: 用石头替换原有物质，把生命的形状保存下来
senses.example: The fallen forest was petrified by mineral water.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的森林被含矿物的水化成了石头。
senses.why: Preservation and loss happen in the same motion.
senses.whyCN: 保存与失去在同一次动作里发生。

senses.title: Terrify
senses.definition: to frighten someone so badly that the body will not obey
senses.definitionCN: 把某人吓到身体不听使唤
senses.example: The sound from the cellar petrified the child.
senses.exampleCN: 地窖里传来的声音把那孩子吓呆了。
senses.why: The figurative sense borrows the literal one: fear turns a person to stone.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义借用了字面义：恐惧把人变成石头。

senses.title: Freeze in place
senses.definition: to leave a person standing still, as if the limbs had hardened
senses.definitionCN: 让人站在原地不动，好像四肢已经变硬
senses.example: She was petrified at the top of the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她在楼梯顶端僵住了。
senses.why: The body's stillness is the whole point of the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 身体的静止正是这个比喻的全部要点。

senses.title: Institutional paralysis
senses.definition: to make an organisation unable to change or to act
senses.definitionCN: 让一个机构无法改变或行动
senses.example: Fear of blame had petrified the department.
senses.exampleCN: 对追责的恐惧让这个部门僵化了。
senses.why: Institutions can be petrified too, and they last longer than people.
senses.whyCN: 机构也会被石化，而且比人持续得更久。

senses.title: Hardening of feeling
senses.definition: to make a feeling or a heart stiff and unyielding
senses.definitionCN: 让一种情感或一颗心变得僵硬、不肯弯折
senses.example: Grief had petrified what was left of their kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 悲伤把他们剩下的善意也硬化了。
senses.why: The word can describe a defence that has outlived its use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以描述一种已经超出用途的防御。

senses.title: Shock into silence
senses.definition: to leave a room or a person unable to speak
senses.definitionCN: 让一个房间或一个人说不出话
senses.example: The verdict petrified the courtroom.
senses.exampleCN: 判决让整个法庭惊呆了。
senses.why: Silence after shock is the social form of standing still.
senses.whyCN: 震惊后的沉默，是僵立的社交版本。

senses.title: Petrifying spring
senses.definition: to encrust objects with stone, as mineral water does
senses.definitionCN: 像含矿物的水那样给物体裹上一层石壳
senses.example: The spring petrified the branches that fell into it.
senses.exampleCN: 那眼泉水把落进去的枝条裹成了石头。
senses.why: Water here does the work that time does elsewhere, only faster.
senses.whyCN: 这里水做的是别处时间做的事，只是快得多。

intro.en: Petrify is rock plus making: the word simply says 'to make stone'.
intro.cn: petrify 是「岩石」加「使成为」：这个词说的就是「使变成石头」。

items.en: Petra meant 'rock or stone', the word behind petrous and petroleum.
items.cn: petra 意为「岩石」，是 petrous 与 petroleum 背后的词。

items.en: Latin kept petra unchanged, and the church built a whole name on it.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样保留 petra，教会还在它上面造出了一整个名号。

items.en: The ending -fy comes from facere, 'to make', as in simplify and solidify.
items.cn: 词尾 -fy 来自 facere（使成为），如 simplify 与 solidify。

items.en: English formed petrify in the sixteenth century for the mineral process.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪造出 petrify，指矿化过程。

items.en: The sense of fright came later: a frightened body behaves like hardened stone.
items.cn: 受惊的义项出现得更晚：受惊的身体像硬了的石头。

note.en: The look-alike group is the petra family; the near-meaning group separates terror, fossilisation and literal hardening.
note.cn: 形近组是 petra 词族；近义组把「恐惧」「化石化」与字面意义上的变硬分开。

entries.definition: turned to stone, or frozen by fear.
entries.definitionCN: 石化的，或被恐惧冻住的。

entries.definition: making someone rigid with fear.
entries.definitionCN: 让人怕到僵住的。

entries.definition: the process of turning to stone.
entries.definitionCN: 变成石头的过程。

entries.definition: turns to stone or freezes another.
entries.definitionCN: 使石化，或使他人僵住。

entries.definition: to fill with great fear.
entries.definitionCN: 使充满巨大恐惧。

entries.definition: to shock with something dreadful.
entries.definitionCN: 以可怕之事使人震惊。

entries.definition: to preserve as a fossil.
entries.definitionCN: 保存为化石。

entries.definition: to turn into bone or become rigid.
entries.definitionCN: 变成骨，或变得僵化。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of mineral water slowly turning a branch into stone.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「含矿物的水把枝条慢慢变成石头」的画面。

normal.en: Petrify holds petra, Greek for rock, and -fy, to make: to make rock.
normal.cn: petrify 里藏着 petra（希腊语的岩石）与 -fy（使成为）：使变成岩石。

normal.en: Think of a branch in a mineral spring: it keeps its shape and loses its wood.
normal.cn: 想象矿物泉里的一根枝条：形状还在，木头没了。

normal.en: Pet-ri-FY: the stress sits on pet, and the rest is the making.
normal.cn: pet-ri-FY：重音落在 pet，其余部分是「使成为」。

normal.en: Say PET-ruh-fye; the first syllable is short, like a tap on stone.
normal.cn: 读成 PET-ruh-fye，第一音节短促，像敲一下石头。

normal.en: Pair it with fear: a frightened witness is a person who has been petrified.
normal.cn: 把它和 fear 配对：被吓住的证人，就是一个被石化的人。

abstract.en: The literal and the figurative senses share one idea: something alive stops moving.
abstract.cn: 字面义与比喻义共享一个想法：活着的东西停止移动。

abstract.en: Stone is what remains when the soft part leaves, which is why the word suits both fossils and fear.
abstract.cn: 石头是柔软部分离开后留下的东西，所以这个词既适合化石也适合恐惧。

abstract.en: An institution can be petrified without any rock at all; it simply stops answering new questions.
abstract.cn: 机构可以没有一点石头也被石化，它只是不再回答新问题。

examples.en: He felt the news petrify him where he stood.
examples.cn: 那条消息把他吓得当场僵住。

examples.en: The fallen forest was petrified by mineral water.
examples.cn: 倒下的森林被含矿物的水化成了石头。

examples.en: Fear of blame had petrified the department.
examples.cn: 对追责的恐惧让这个部门僵化了。

dict_mnemonic.text: petri（岩石）+ fy（使成为）：使变成石头，人被吓到也会「僵成石头」。

root: 希腊语 petra（岩石）经拉丁语 petra 进入英语，加 -fy（使成为，源自 facere）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all end in stillness: mineral replacement, a fossil, a frightened body, a frozen posture, a stuck institution, a hardened heart, a silent court and a spring that coats whatever falls in.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都以静止收尾：矿物替换、化石、受惊的身体、僵住的姿势、卡住的机构、硬化的心、无声的法庭与一眼给落物裹壳的泉。

core.en: A BRANCH THAT KEEPS ITS SHAPE AND LOSES ITS WOOD
core.cn: 保住形状、失去木质的枝条

branches.en: Stone replacing wood, slowly.
branches.cn: 石头缓慢地替换木头。

branches.en: A frightened body that will not obey.
branches.cn: 不听使唤的受惊身体。

branches.en: A stuck institution and a hardened heart.
branches.cn: 卡住的机构与硬化的心。

branches.en: A room that has gone silent.
branches.cn: 一个静下来的房间。

branches.en: Water doing in a year what time does in an age.
branches.cn: 水在一年里做时间在一个纪元里做的事。

intro.en: The petra family is about rock: petrous describes the hard bone at the base of the skull, petroleum is rock oil, and petrify is rock-making.
intro.cn: petra 词族关乎岩石：petrous 描述颅底的硬骨，petroleum 是岩中之油，petrify 是造石。

latinIntro.en: Greek petra passes into Latin unchanged, and the suffix -ficare, from facere, supplies the 'making' in every -fy verb.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 petra 原样进入拉丁语，而来自 facere 的后缀 -ficare 为每个 -fy 动词提供「使成为」。

definition_zh: 由……构成；由……组成；包括；由……构成其全部内容
definition_en: to be made up of the parts, members or items that are named after the preposition
core_image: 一只木盒被倒过来，零件一件件落在桌面上，排成一列，正好凑成盒子里原来装着的那件东西
scene: 检验员把一台旧仪器拆开，把里面的零件按大小排成一列，逐一登记。 The device should consist of a lens, a brass tube and a wooden stand.
sceneCN: 这里指一台装置由若干部件构成（第 1 个义项：整体由列出的部分组成）；句意为一台这样的装置应由一片透镜、一根黄铜管与一个木架构成。图中可辨识物件：拆开的仪器、排成一列的零件、登记簿、木架。

pos.zh: 由……构成（及物动词短语，后接构成整体的各部分）
由……组成（后接成员、成分或步骤）

collocations.phrase: consist of a summary and an appendix

derivatives.zh: 由同根形容词加名词尾构成，义为「一致性」，与「构成」义不同
由同根词干加形容词尾构成，义为「一致的」，与「构成」义不同
由同根形容词加副词尾构成，义为「一贯地」
由否定前缀加同根形容词构成，义为「不一致的」

senses.title: Made of physical parts
senses.definition: to be built from a stated set of components
senses.definitionCN: 由一组明确的部件搭成
senses.example: The bridge must consist of three spans and a central pier.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥必须由三个跨度与一座中央桥墩构成。
senses.why: The core verb meant to stand together; parts that stand together make one whole, which is the oldest sense of the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词本义是「站在一起」；站在一起的各部分合成一个整体，这正是短语最古老的义项。

senses.title: Composed of members
senses.definition: to have a stated set of people as its members
senses.definitionCN: 以一组明确的人作为其成员
senses.example: The panel should consist of five reviewers from outside the university.
senses.exampleCN: 评审小组应由五名校外评审人组成。
senses.why: Parts that stand together can be people; a panel is a whole made of named members.
senses.whyCN: 站在一起的部分也可以是人；小组就是由具名成员构成的整体。

senses.title: Made of ingredients
senses.definition: to be made from a stated mixture of materials
senses.definitionCN: 由明确的材料混合物制成
senses.example: The plaster can consist of lime, sand and animal hair.
senses.exampleCN: 这种灰泥可以由石灰、砂与动物毛构成。
senses.why: The standing-together image applies to a mixture: the materials stand in one body.
senses.whyCN: 「站在一起」的意象也用于混合物：材料站进同一个身体。

senses.title: Divided into steps
senses.definition: to be carried out as a stated series of stages
senses.definitionCN: 按明确的一系列阶段进行
senses.example: The procedure must consist of four washes and one final rinse.
senses.exampleCN: 该流程必须由四次洗涤与最后一次漂洗构成。
senses.why: Stages stand one after another in a procedure and together make the whole.
senses.whyCN: 各阶段在流程中依次站住，共同构成整体。

senses.title: Built from chapters or sections
senses.definition: to be organised as a stated set of sections
senses.definitionCN: 按明确的一组章节组织起来
senses.example: The report should consist of a summary, three chapters and an appendix.
senses.exampleCN: 报告应由一篇摘要、三章正文与一个附录构成。
senses.why: Sections stand together in a fixed order to make one report.
senses.whyCN: 各章节按固定次序站在一起，构成一份报告。

senses.title: Made of elements or compounds
senses.definition: to be composed of stated chemical constituents
senses.definitionCN: 由明确的化学组分构成
senses.example: The mineral may consist of iron oxide with traces of silica.
senses.exampleCN: 这种矿物可能由氧化铁并含微量二氧化硅组成。
senses.why: Chemical constituents stand together in one mineral.
senses.whyCN: 化学组分在同一块矿物中站在一起。

senses.title: Made of premises
senses.definition: to be constructed from stated assumptions or statements
senses.definitionCN: 由明确的假设或陈述搭成
senses.example: A valid proof must consist of premises that are either given or already shown.
senses.exampleCN: 一个有效的证明必须由已给出或已证明的命题构成。
senses.why: Premises stand together to hold up one conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 各前提站在一起，托住一个结论。

senses.title: Accounted for by budget items
senses.definition: to be made up of stated categories of spending
senses.definitionCN: 由明确的支出类别构成
senses.example: The annual budget can consist of salaries, maintenance and a small reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 年度预算可由薪金、维护费与一小笔储备构成。
senses.why: Spending lines stand together to make one annual sum.
senses.whyCN: 各支出项目站在一起，构成一个年度总额。

senses.title: Made up of stated proportions
senses.definition: to be made up of stated proportions of a population or a set
senses.definitionCN: 按明确的比例由某一群体或集合构成
senses.example: The sample must consist of equal numbers of men and women.
senses.exampleCN: 样本必须由数目相等的男性与女性构成。
senses.why: A sample can be a whole whose parts stand in a stated ratio.
senses.whyCN: 样本可以是一个整体，其各部分按明确比例站在一起。

intro.en: The phrase is built on a Latin verb meaning to stand together. Parts that stand together form a whole, and English uses the phrase to name exactly those parts, never the whole itself as one of them.
intro.cn: 这个短语建立在拉丁语「一起站立」的动词上。站在一起的各部分构成整体，英语正是用这个短语点出这些部分，而绝不把整体本身算作其中一个部分。

items.en: Sistere meant to stand or to place, and it supplied the standing image for the whole family.
items.cn: 这个词意为「站立、安放」，为整个词族提供了「站立」的意象。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus sistere produced consistere, to stand together, to hold firm, to be made up of.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的前缀加「站立」，构成「站在一起、立稳、由……构成」的动词。

items.en: French passed the verb to English in the sixteenth century, where it first meant to have a certain nature or makeup.
items.cn: 法语在十六世纪把这个动词传给英语，最初指「具有某种本性或构造」。

items.en: Two prepositions split the old verb: of names the parts, in names the essential point. The pair is a frequent source of error.
items.cn: 两个介词把这个古老动词一分为二：一个点出部分，另一个点出实质所在。这对搭配是常见的错误来源。

items.en: The frame with this preposition became the standard way to list the parts of a whole. The exact first citation and the date of the split from the other preposition are uncertain.
items.cn: 与这个介词搭配的框架成为列举整体各部分的标准说法。最早书证年代，以及它与另一介词用法分化的年代，均不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin standing root and is constantly confused with the phrase; the second group holds other ways of naming the parts of a whole.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁「站立」词根，常与本短语混淆；第二组是其他列举整体部分的说法。

entries.definition: It means to agree with something, not to be made up of it. A report can be consistent with the evidence while consisting of five chapters.
entries.definitionCN: 它的意思是「与某物一致」，而不是「由某物构成」。一份报告可以合乎证据，同时由五章构成。

entries.definition: It names the essential point rather than the parts, as when a method consists in careful measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 它点出实质所在，而非列举部分，例如某方法实质在于仔细测量。

entries.definition: It names agreement or evenness, not the parts of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 它指「一致性、均匀」，而不是整体的各部分。

entries.definition: The adjective describes agreement, so it cannot replace the phrase when parts are being listed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词描述「一致」，因此在列举部分时不能替换本短语。

entries.definition: A formal equivalent that stresses the act of putting parts together; it is common in technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的对应说法，强调把部分合在一起的动作，常见于技术写作。

entries.definition: It usually takes the whole as subject and the parts as object; usage guides disagree about the reverse pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 通常以整体作主语、部分作宾语；用法指南对反过来用的写法意见不一。

entries.definition: The everyday equivalent; it works in speech where the phrase would sound too formal.
entries.definitionCN: 日常对应说法，在口语中比本短语自然。

entries.definition: It reverses the direction: the parts constitute the whole, so the whole is not the subject.
entries.definitionCN: 方向相反：部分构成整体，因此整体不能作主语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the tipped box, the five reviewers, the plaster mix and the budget sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用倒出的木盒、五名评审、灰泥配料与预算表四个场景。

normal.en: A box tipped over: the parts fall out and line up into exactly the thing that was inside.
normal.cn: 木盒一倒，零件落出来排成一列，正好凑成原来装在里面的那件东西。

normal.en: Five reviewers from outside the university, no more and no fewer.
normal.cn: 五名校外评审，不多也不少。

normal.en: Lime, sand and animal hair mixed into plaster.
normal.cn: 石灰、砂与动物毛拌成灰泥。

normal.en: Four washes and one rinse, in that order.
normal.cn: 四次洗涤加一次漂洗，顺序不能乱。

normal.en: A budget with three lines and a small reserve.
normal.cn: 预算只有三行，再加一小笔储备。

abstract.en: The phrase names the parts and never lets the whole join the list.
abstract.cn: 这个短语只点部分，绝不让整体混进清单。

abstract.en: A whole is not one of its own parts, just as a sentence is not one of its words.
abstract.cn: 整体不是自己的一个部分，正如句子不是它的某个词。

abstract.en: Two prepositions from one verb: one lists the pieces, the other names the point.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词配两个介词：一个列零件，一个点实质。

examples.en: The committee should consist of seven members with voting rights.
examples.cn: 该委员会应由七名有表决权的成员组成。

examples.en: The atmosphere must consist of nitrogen, oxygen and a few trace gases.
examples.cn: 大气必须由氮、氧与少数微量气体构成。

examples.en: A good lecture can consist of one question and three examples.
examples.cn: 一堂好课可以由一个问题与三个例子构成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「肯西斯特 欧夫」：把「站在一起」记成倒出来的零件排成一列，正好拼回原物——零件站着，整体就成了

root: 核心动词出自拉丁语，由表示「一起」的前缀加表示「站立」的词根构成，本义是「站在一起、立稳」，引申为「由若干部分合成整体」。该短语后接介词引出各部分，整体本身不能列入其中。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses name parts of different wholes: components, members, ingredients, steps, chapters, chemical constituents, premises, budget lines, and proportions.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项为不同的整体点名部分：部件、成员、成分、步骤、章节、化学组分、前提、预算项目与比例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a box tipped over, its parts falling out and lining up into exactly the object that had been inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：木盒被倒过来，零件落出排成一列，正好拼成原来装在里面的那件东西。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL WHOLE: components, ingredients and chemical constituents are all matter arranged into one object.
branches.cn: 物质整体：部件、成分与化学组分都是被排成一件物体的物质。

branches.en: THE COUNTED WHOLE: people on a panel and lines in a budget are both lists that must add up.
branches.cn: 可数的整体：评审名单与预算条目都是必须加得起来的清单。

branches.en: THE ORDERED WHOLE: steps in a procedure and sections in a report follow a sequence.
branches.cn: 有序的整体：流程步骤与报告章节都按顺序排列。

branches.en: THE LOGICAL WHOLE: a proof is built out of premises that already stand.
branches.cn: 逻辑整体：证明由已经站得住的前提搭成。

branches.en: THE PROPORTIONAL WHOLE: a sample is built to a stated ratio.
branches.cn: 比例整体：样本按明确比例构成。

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin standing verb; the same stem gives both the phrase of composition and the adjective of agreement.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语「站立」动词上；同一个词干既造出「构成」短语，也造出「一致」形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin consistere passed through French into English, and the preposition of was added in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「一起站立」经法语进入英语，介词部分则是英语后加的。

items.example: It marks the parts as standing in one place.
items.exampleCN: 它标出各部分站到同一处。

items.example: It introduces the parts that make the whole.
items.exampleCN: 它引出构成整体的各部分。

definition_zh: v. 竞争，争夺；主张，坚称；应对，抗争
definition_en: to compete for something, or to argue that something is true
core_image: 两方各拉一端，绳子绷得笔直
scene: 十支队伍争夺同一个奖杯。 Ten teams contend for the same cup.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：contend 指争夺；句意是十支队伍争夺同一个奖杯。

pos.zh: 竞争；主张；抗争

senses.title: Struggle for a prize
senses.definition: to compete with others for something
senses.definitionCN: 与他人争夺某物
senses.example: Ten teams contend for the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 十支队伍争夺奖杯。
senses.why: Latin contendere means to stretch with others.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 contendere 意为与他人一同用力。

senses.title: Argue as true
senses.definition: to state firmly that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地认为某事为真
senses.example: He contends that the rule is unfair.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚称这条规则不公。
senses.why: The tug of words replaces the tug of ropes.
senses.whyCN: 言语的拉扯取代了绳索的拉扯。

senses.title: Struggle against
senses.definition: to have to deal with a difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 不得不应付困难
senses.example: She had to contend with noise.
senses.exampleCN: 她不得不应付噪音。
senses.why: The contest turns into endurance.
senses.whyCN: 竞争变成了耐力。

intro.en: Contend is Latin contendere, to stretch with another.
intro.cn: contend 是拉丁语 contendere，意为与他人一同绷紧用力。

items.en: Tendere means to stretch.
items.cn: tendere 意为拉伸。

items.en: Contendere means to stretch with others.
items.cn: contendere 意为与他人一同用力。

items.en: Contentio names the struggle.
items.cn: contentio 指争斗。

items.en: English used contend of battle.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语用它指战斗。

items.en: Law used contend of arguing a case.
items.cn: 十七世纪法律用它指论辩案件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the contend- stem; the near-meaning group names competing and arguing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 contend- 词干；近义组列出竞争与论辩。

entries.definition: An argument or claim.
entries.definitionCN: 争论或主张。

entries.definition: Likely to cause disagreement.
entries.definitionCN: 易引起争论的。

entries.definition: A person competing for something.
entries.definitionCN: 争夺某物的人。

entries.definition: To try to win against others.
entries.definitionCN: 与他人争胜。

entries.definition: To give reasons for a view.
entries.definitionCN: 为观点给理由。

entries.definition: To try hard against difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 竭力对付困难。

entries.definition: To keep saying something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持某说法。

normalIntro.en: To contend is to pull hard, whether on a rope or on an argument.
normalIntro.cn: contend 就是用力拉，无论拉绳还是拉道理。

normal.en: Tendere means to stretch.
normal.cn: tendere 意为拉伸。

normal.en: Contendere means to strain with others.
normal.cn: contendere 意为与他人一并用力。

normal.cn: 各队争夺同一座杯。

normal.en: Lawyers contend that a rule is unfair.
normal.cn: 律师主张某规则不公。

normal.en: You contend with noise and with rivals.
normal.cn: 你既与噪音周旋，也与对手较量。

abstract.cn: 被两边拉得笔直的绳。

abstract.en: A runner leaning at the line.

branches.en: Teams chasing one cup.

definition_zh: n. 大块，厚块；（口语）相当大的部分
definition_en: a thick solid piece; a large amount or part of something
core_image: 掰开的面包露出厚厚的一块
scene: 他把面包掰成几大块分给孩子。 He broke the bread into chunks for the children.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chunk 指大块；句意是他把面包掰成几大块分给孩子。

pos.zh: 大块；相当大的一部分

senses.title: A thick piece
senses.definition: a thick solid piece cut or broken from something larger
senses.definitionCN: 从较大物体上切下或掰下的厚块
senses.example: He dropped a chunk of ice into the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 他往杯里丢了一块冰。
senses.why: The word is probably a variant of chuck, a lump.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能是 chuck（一块）的变体。

senses.title: A large part
senses.definition: a large amount or portion of something abstract
senses.definitionCN: 某事物中相当大的数量或部分
senses.example: A chunk of the budget went on repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 预算的很大一部分花在维修上。
senses.why: The solid sense loosened into an amount.
senses.whyCN: 实物的「块」松动成了数量。

intro.en: Chunk appears in the seventeenth century, probably as a variant of chuck, a lump.
intro.cn: chunk 于十七世纪出现，很可能是 chuck（一块）的变体。

items.en: Chunk first names a thick lump.
items.cn: 十七世纪 chunk 指厚块。

items.en: A chunk of bread or meat is common.

items.en: Chunk means a large part of anything.

entries.definition: A part cut from something.

entries.definition: A large solid piece with flat sides.

normalIntro.en: A chunk is the piece you can hold in one hand.
normalIntro.cn: chunk 是一只手能握住的那一块。

normal.en: Chunk sounds like chuck, a lump.

normal.en: It is a thick solid piece.

normal.en: Bread breaks into chunks.

normal.en: Ice falls in chunks.

abstract.en: A handful of something solid.
abstract.cn: 一把实实在在的东西。

abstract.en: The budget cut into pieces.

examples.cn: 墙上有一块塌落了。

examples.en: He spends a chunk of each day reading.
examples.cn: 他每天花一大段时间阅读。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a lump of solid matter and loosens into any large part.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一块固体起家，后来松动成任何大部分。

branches.en: Bread torn into rough pieces.
branches.cn: 撕成粗块的面包。

branches.en: A slice of the budget marked off.
branches.cn: 被划出的一块预算。

definition_zh: 刺激的复数形式：多个刺激或一组刺激系列，用于实验心理学、神经科学与经济刺激措施的复数表达
definition_en: the plural of stimulus, naming several stimuli or a series of them in experiments, neuroscience and policy
core_image: 实验屏同时亮起三种颜色的方块，每种颜色对应一次不同的按键，记录纸上并排出现三列计数
scene: 屏幕同时亮起三种颜色的方块，每种颜色对应一次不同按键，记录纸上并排列出三列。 The task delivered visual and auditory stimuli at fixed intervals.
sceneCN: 这里指同时呈现的多个刺激（第 2 个义项：实验中的多重刺激系列）；句意为任务按固定间隔给出视觉与听觉刺激。

pos.zh: 刺激的复数（stimulus 的规则复数）

derivatives.zh: stimuli 的基础词 stimulus + 拉丁第二变格法 -us 变 -i（复数词尾替换）→ 由单数转为复数形式
stimulate + -ion（动作或结果）→ 刺激作用
stimulare + -ant（施动者）→ 起刺激作用的物质，语义偏移为「兴奋剂」
stimulate + -ive（具有……性质的）→ 有刺激作用的

senses.title: The regular plural of stimulus
senses.definition: the form used for more than one stimulus, keeping the Latin second-declension pattern -us to -i
senses.definitionCN: 指一个以上刺激时使用的形式，保留拉丁第二变格法 -us 变 -i 的规律
senses.example: One stimulus was faint, but the paired stimuli were easy to detect.
senses.exampleCN: 单个刺激很微弱，但成对的刺激很容易被察觉。
senses.why: English borrowed the whole Latin noun and kept its plural, so the form is grammar rather than a new word.
senses.whyCN: 英语整体借入这个拉丁名词并保留其复数，因此这个形式属于语法变化，而非新词。

senses.title: A series of stimuli in an experiment
senses.titleCN: 实验中成系列呈现的多个刺激
senses.definition: several controlled cues presented in sequence so that responses can be compared across trials
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序呈现的多个受控提示，使各轮反应可以比较
senses.example: The programme presented stimuli in random order to prevent guessing.
senses.exampleCN: 程序随机呈现刺激，以防受试者猜测。
senses.why: an experiment rarely uses one cue, so the plural became the normal unit of a trial list.
senses.whyCN: 实验很少只用一个提示，因此复数形式成了试次清单的常规单位。

senses.title: Sensory inputs taken together
senses.titleCN: 被一起接收的多种感官输入
senses.definition: the combined light, sound, smell, taste and touch reaching the senses at one time
senses.definitionCN: 同一时间到达感官的光、声、气味、味道与触感的总体
senses.example: The brain must separate relevant stimuli from background noise.
senses.exampleCN: 大脑必须把相关刺激从背景噪声中分出来。
senses.why: senses never receive one channel at a time, so the plural names the ordinary condition.
senses.whyCN: 感官从不同时只接收一个通道，因此复数命名的才是常态。

senses.title: Multichannel stimulation in neuroscience
senses.titleCN: 神经科学中的多通道刺激
senses.definition: several electrical or sensory channels activated together in a controlled pattern
senses.definitionCN: 按受控模式同时激活的多个电或感官通道
senses.example: Electrode arrays delivered stimuli to several sites at once.
senses.exampleCN: 电极阵列同时向多个位点施加刺激。
senses.why: modern equipment can address many channels, and the Latin plural was already available.
senses.whyCN: 现代设备能同时作用于多个通道，而拉丁复数早已现成。

senses.title: Several policy stimuli
senses.definition: more than one measure, such as spending and tax cuts, intended to move an economy
senses.definitionCN: 支出与减税等一项以上的措施，旨在推动经济
senses.example: The budget combined fiscal and monetary stimuli.
senses.exampleCN: 预算把财政与货币刺激组合起来。
senses.why: economists treat each measure as a prod, so a package is naturally plural.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把每项措施当作一次戳动，因此一揽子措施自然用复数。

senses.title: Several spurs to action
senses.titleCN: 多种促使人行动的因素
senses.definition: multiple things that incite a person or group to act, create or think
senses.definitionCN: 促使个人或群体行动、创造或思考的多个事物
senses.example: Awards and travel grants were the stimuli behind the new programme.
senses.exampleCN: 奖项与差旅资助是新项目背后的多重推动。
senses.why: the figurative sense also pluralises, because motives rarely come one at a time.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义同样有复数，因为动机很少一次只来一个。

senses.title: A stimulus array in methods
senses.titleCN: 研究方法术语中的刺激阵列
senses.definition: a defined set of stimuli treated as one display or one block in a study
senses.definitionCN: 研究中被当作一个显示或一个区组的既定刺激集合
senses.example: The stimulus array contained forty faces and twenty houses.
senses.exampleCN: 刺激阵列包含四十张面孔与二十座房屋。
senses.why: method writers needed a name for the whole set, and the plural supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 方法学作者需要给整个集合一个名字，复数形式正好提供。

senses.title: The spelling and pronunciation to watch
senses.titleCN: 复数拼写与读音的用法提醒
senses.definition: the plural is written stimuli and pronounced with a final long i, never as a singular
senses.definitionCN: 复数写作 stimuli，词尾读长音 i，不可当作单数使用
senses.example: Writing 'a stimuli' is a common error in student reports.
senses.exampleCN: 在学生的报告里写 a stimuli 是常见错误。
senses.why: because the Latin ending is unusual, the plural is often mistaken for a singular, which is why the usage point belongs here.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个拉丁词尾不常见，复数常被误当作单数，因此这条用法提醒也应算一个义项。

intro.en: Stimuli is not a separate coinage but the Latin plural of stimulus, kept intact in technical English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stimuli 不是另造的单词，而是 stimulus 的拉丁复数，在技术英语中整体保留。年代为约数。

items.en: Masculine nouns ending in -us normally take -i in the nominative plural, so stimulus 'goad' becomes stimuli 'goads'.
items.cn: 以 -us 结尾的阳性名词，主格复数通常把词尾变为 -i，因此 stimulus「刺棒」的复数是 stimuli「多根刺棒」。

items.en: The singular named a goad or spur, a pointed tool for driving animals, and by extension anything that incites.
items.cn: 单数指刺棒或马刺，即驱赶牲畜的尖头工具，并引申为任何激起行动之物。

items.en: The verb stimulare 'to goad, urge on' belongs to the same family and gave English stimulate.
items.cn: 动词 stimulare「驱赶、催促」属于同一词族，并给出英语 stimulate。

items.en: Scientific English of the seventeenth to nineteenth centuries kept Latin plurals for learned nouns, which is how stimuli survived beside the English word.
items.cn: 17 至 19 世纪的科学英语为学术名词保留拉丁复数，stimuli 因此与英语词并存。

items.en: Psychology, physiology and economics made stimuli routine: paired stimuli in a trial list, multichannel stimuli in a laboratory, fiscal stimuli in a budget.
items.cn: 心理学、生理学与经济学使 stimuli 成为常规用法：试次清单里的成对刺激、实验室里的多通道刺激、预算里的财政刺激。

items.en: Reconstructed form (deeper root of the singular): the link to an Indo-European root for 'to prick' is a hypothesis, and every form proposed for that root is a reconstruction; the plural ending itself follows a documented Latin declension.
items.cn: 重构形式（单数形式的更深词根）：与印欧语「刺、扎」词根的联系只是假说，为该词根提出的形式全是重构；复数词尾本身则遵循有书证的拉丁变格法。

note.en: Group one holds the singular and the near-spellings that are often swapped for the plural; group two holds other plural nouns of input and inducement.
note.cn: 第一组是单数与常被误换成复数的近形词；第二组是同样表示输入与诱因的其他复数名词。

entries.definition: The singular form for one cue; using it where several are meant is the commonest error in the pair.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个提示的单数形式；在该用复数处用它，是这一对词里最常见的错误。

entries.definition: A drug or drink that raises bodily activity; it is consumed, while stimuli are presented.
entries.definitionCN: 提高身体活动的药物或饮料，是被摄入的；stimuli 是被呈现的。

entries.definition: The verb meaning 'to apply a stimulus'; it cannot stand where a plural noun is required.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「施加刺激」的动词，不能用在需要复数名词的位置。

entries.definition: Signals that tell someone when or what to do; cues are usually deliberate, while stimuli may simply occur.
entries.definitionCN: 告诉人何时或做什么的信号；提示通常是有意的，而刺激可以只是发生。

entries.definition: Whatever enters a system, machine or process; the word is neutral about whether a response follows.
entries.definitionCN: 进入系统、机器或过程的一切；这个词不保证随后会有反应。

entries.definition: Rewards offered to make people act; they work through desire rather than through direct evocation.
entries.definitionCN: 为让人行动而提供的奖励，通过欲望起作用，而非直接引发反应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, real experimental collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的形态变化、真实实验搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One -us becomes many -i: the ending itself carries the plural.
normal.cn: 一个 -us 变成多个 -i：词尾本身就带着复数信息。

normal.en: The singular is the goad, and the plural is several goads at once.
normal.cn: 单数是那根刺棒，复数是同时落下的几根。

normal.en: The family runs stimulus, stimuli, stimulate, stimulation, stimulant.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 stimulus、stimuli、stimulate、stimulation、stimulant。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the laboratory: paired stimuli, competing stimuli, visual and auditory stimuli.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出实验室用法：成对刺激、相互竞争的刺激、视觉与听觉刺激。

normal.en: In policy talk the plural is normal: fiscal and monetary stimuli.
normal.cn: 政策话语里复数很常见：财政与货币刺激。

abstract.en: Picture three coloured squares lighting at once and three columns of tallies appearing.
abstract.cn: 想象三个彩色方块同时亮起，三列计数同时出现。

abstract.en: Picture many small taps arriving on one skin at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象许多轻触在同一刻落到同一块皮肤上。

abstract.en: Picture a single switch multiplied into a panel of switches.
abstract.cn: 想象一个开关扩展成一整块开关面板。

examples.en: The infants were shown paired stimuli until their gaze shifted.
examples.cn: 研究者给婴儿看成对的刺激，直到他们的注视转移。

examples.en: Competing stimuli made the task far harder than the pilot study.
examples.cn: 相互竞争的刺激使任务比预试困难得多。

examples.en: The central bank announced two separate stimuli within one quarter.
examples.cn: 央行在一个季度内宣布了两项独立的刺激措施。

dict_mnemonic.text: stimulus 的复数按拉丁第二变格法变 -us 为 -i；记「一根刺棒，一把刺棒」。

root: 拉丁 stimulus「刺棒、尖刺」的复数 stimuli；拉丁第二变格法阳性名词 -us 变 -i，英语技术文献整体保留该复数。更早词源不确定，与印欧语「刺、扎」词根的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one plural form: grammar first, then series in experiments, sensory streams, multichannel stimulation, policy packages, several motives, arrays in methods and a usage warning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个复数形式展开：先是语法，再是实验中的系列、感官流、多通道刺激、政策组合、多重动机、方法学阵列，最后是一条用法提醒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one goad multiplied into a panel of goads arriving together.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根刺棒扩展成一整块同时落下的刺棒面板。

branches.en: THE FORM: the plural exists first as Latin grammar, not as a new meaning.
branches.cn: 形式：这个复数首先作为拉丁语法存在，而不是新的意义。

branches.en: TRIALS AND SENSES: a list of cues and a stream of sensory input are both plural by nature.
branches.cn: 试次与感官：提示清单与感官输入流在本质上都是复数。

branches.en: LABORATORY SETS: multichannel stimulation and a defined stimulus array are the same plural seen as equipment and as method.
branches.cn: 实验室集合：多通道刺激与既定刺激阵列，是同一复数在设备与方法两个层面的表现。

branches.en: MEASURES AND MOTIVES: a policy package and several spurs to action both prod more than once.
branches.cn: 措施与动机：一揽子政策与多重推动，都不止戳动一次。

branches.en: THE WARNING: because the ending is Latin, the plural is often misread as a singular.
branches.cn: 提醒：由于词尾是拉丁式，复数常被误读作单数。

intro.en: Stimuli has no separate suffixes of its own; it is the plural inflection of stimulus, so the family is read through the singular stem.
intro.cn: stimuli 本身没有独立后缀，它是 stimulus 的复数屈折形式，因此整个词族要经由单数词干来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin stimulus and stimulare supply the stem, and the second-declension ending -i supplies the plural; English then added -ate, -ion, -ive and -ant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stimulus 与 stimulare 提供词干，第二变格法词尾 -i 提供复数；英语随后加了 -ate、-ion、-ive 与 -ant。

items.example: The singular is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 单数是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The ending alone tells a reader that several are meant.
items.exampleCN: 仅这个词尾就告诉读者所指的是多个。

items.example: The verb supplies the English verb forms.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供英语的动词形式。

items.example: The verb is built on the same stem as the plural.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词与复数形式同干。

items.example: The noun often names a laboratory procedure.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词常指一种实验室操作。

items.example: The noun narrowed to drugs and drinks.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词收窄到药物与饮料。

items.example: The adjective is frequent in policy writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在政策写作中常见。

items.meaning: one or a device that stimulates
items.example: Medical devices often carry this name.
items.exampleCN: 医疗装置常用这个名称。

items.example: The Latin noun is the model for the English action noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是英语动作名词的模板。

definition_zh: n. 二氧化物；（气候语境）二氧化碳
definition_en: an oxide whose formula contains two oxygen atoms, especially carbon dioxide
core_image: 化学式右下角那个小小的二；手持检测仪的数字屏在车流旁往上跳
scene: 仪器显示二氧化碳读数偏高。 The meter shows a high dioxide reading.
sceneCN: 这里 dioxide 在气候语境里是「二氧化碳」的简称（第 2 个义项）；句意是仪器显示二氧化碳读数偏高。图中可辨识物件：手持检测仪、跳动的数字屏、半开的窗与窗外车流。

pos.zh: 二氧化物；（气候语境）二氧化碳

senses.title: Two oxygen atoms
senses.definition: an oxide whose formula unit contains two oxygen atoms
senses.definitionCN: （名词）化学式单元中含两个氧原子的氧化物
senses.example: Sulphur dioxide fell sharply after the filters were fitted.
senses.exampleCN: 装上过滤器后二氧化硫大幅下降。
senses.why: A formula on a card with a small two written at the lower right.
senses.whyCN: 卡片上的化学式，右下角写着一个小小的二。

senses.title: Carbon dioxide for short
senses.definition: carbon dioxide, when the context makes the first word unnecessary
senses.definitionCN: （名词）上下文已明确时省略 carbon 的二氧化碳
senses.example: The meter shows a high dioxide reading.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器显示二氧化碳读数偏高。
senses.why: A handheld meter whose digits climb beside a busy road.
senses.whyCN: 一台手持检测仪，在车流旁数字往上跳。

senses.title: An output to be cut
senses.definition: such a gas treated as an emission to be measured or reduced
senses.definitionCN: （名词）被当作需要计量或削减的排放物的这类气体
senses.example: The plant cut its dioxide output by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把二氧化物排放量削减了三分之一。
senses.why: A chimney with a clamp-on sensor and a falling line on a chart.
senses.whyCN: 一根烟囱夹着传感器，图表上的线往下走。

intro.en: Dioxide joins Greek di- twice to oxide, a French coinage from oxygène and acide, whose oxy- comes from Greek oxys, sharp or acid.
intro.cn: dioxide 把希腊语 di-（二）与 oxide 拼在一起；oxide 是法语用 oxygène 与 acide 造的词，其中 oxy- 来自希腊语 oxys（尖的、酸的）。

items.en: Di- meant twice.
items.cn: di- 意为两次。

items.en: Oxys meant sharp or acid.
items.cn: oxys 意为尖的、酸的。

items.en: Genes meant born or producing.
items.cn: genes 意为产生的。

items.en: French coined oxide from oxygène and acide.
items.cn: 十八世纪法语用 oxygène 与 acide 造出 oxide。

items.en: Dioxide named a compound with two oxygens.
items.cn: 十九世纪 dioxide 指含两个氧的化合物。

items.en: Carbon dioxide became the headline gas.
items.cn: 二十世纪二氧化碳成了头条气体。

note.en: The look-alike group counts oxygen atoms; the near-meaning group names what such gases become in the air.
note.cn: 形近组按氧原子个数区分；近义组是这类气体进入空气后的身份。

entries.definition: A compound of oxygen with another element.
entries.definitionCN: 氧与另一种元素的化合物。

entries.definition: A compound with a single oxygen atom.
entries.definitionCN: 只含一个氧原子的化合物。

entries.definition: The ordinary oxygen molecule, two atoms joined.
entries.definitionCN: 普通的氧分子，两个原子相连。

entries.definition: Something discharged, especially gas.
entries.definitionCN: 排出的东西，尤指气体。

entries.definition: A substance that makes air or water dirty.
entries.definitionCN: 使空气或水变脏的物质。

entries.definition: A gas that traps heat in the atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 在大气中留住热量的气体。

normalIntro.en: Dioxide is di- two plus oxide: read the little two at the bottom right of the formula.
normalIntro.cn: dioxide 就是 di-（二）加 oxide：看化学式右下角那个小小的二。

normal.en: Di- two plus oxide means two oxygens in the formula.
normal.cn: di-（二）加 oxide 就是式子里两个氧。

normal.en: Carbon dioxide is the gas plants take in.
normal.cn: 二氧化碳是植物吸收的气体。

normal.en: Monoxide has one oxygen, dioxide has two.
normal.cn: monoxide 一个氧，dioxide 两个氧。

normal.en: Oxide is the family name.
normal.cn: oxide 是家族名。

normal.en: In climate talk dioxide usually means carbon dioxide.
normal.cn: 气候话题里 dioxide 通常指二氧化碳。

abstract.en: A formula on a card with a small two written at the lower right.
abstract.cn: 卡片上的化学式，右下角写着一个小小的二。

abstract.en: A handheld meter whose digits climb beside a busy road.
abstract.cn: 一台手持检测仪，在车流旁数字往上跳。

abstract.en: A chimney with a clamp-on sensor and a falling line on a chart.
abstract.cn: 一根烟囱夹着传感器，图表上的线往下走。

examples.en: The meter shows a high dioxide reading.
examples.cn: 仪器显示二氧化碳读数偏高。

examples.en: Sulphur dioxide fell sharply after the filters were fitted.
examples.cn: 装上过滤器后二氧化硫大幅下降。

examples.en: The plant cut its dioxide output by a third.
examples.cn: 工厂把二氧化物排放量削减了三分之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: dioxide ＝ di-（二）＋ oxide（氧化物，oxy- 来自希腊语 oxys「尖、酸」）＝式子里有两个氧，「二氧化物」。carbon dioxide 是二氧化碳，sulphur dioxide 是二氧化硫；只有一个氧的叫 monoxide。

root: 希腊语 di-（二）＋ 法语 oxide（oxygène「氧」＋ acide「酸」，oxy- 源自希腊语 oxys「尖、酸」）→ 英语 dioxide

sensesIntro.en: A small two in the formula: a written molecule, a climbing meter and a chimney being measured.
sensesIntro.cn: 化学式里那个小小的二：写下的分子、往上爬的读数，以及一根正在被计量的烟囱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small two written at the lower right of a formula while a meter beside the road climbs
core.cn: 核心意象：化学式右下角写着一个小小的二，路边检测仪的数字同时往上爬

branches.en: A formula on a card with a small two written at the lower right.
branches.cn: 卡片上的化学式，右下角写着一个小小的二。

branches.en: A handheld meter whose digits climb beside a busy road.
branches.cn: 一台手持检测仪，在车流旁数字往上跳。

branches.en: A chimney with a clamp-on sensor and a falling line on a chart.
branches.cn: 一根烟囱夹着传感器，图表上的线往下走。

branches.en: The written two becomes a number on a screen.
branches.cn: 写下来的二变成了屏幕上的数字。

branches.en: Both turn the gas into something to be managed.
branches.cn: 两者都把气体变成需要管理的对象。

intro.en: Dioxide is di- plus oxide; the counting prefixes give monoxide and trioxide, and the sharp root gives oxygen.
intro.cn: dioxide 由 di- 加 oxide 构成；计数前缀给出 monoxide 与 trioxide，尖酸这个词根给出 oxygen。

latinIntro.en: Greek oxys means sharp or acid and genes producing; Latin mittere means to send.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 oxys 意为尖的、酸的，genes 意为产生的；拉丁语 mittere 意为送出。

definition_zh: 进化论者；支持进化论的人；（作定语）进化论的
definition_en: a person who accepts or advocates the theory of biological evolution
core_image: 一位学者站在挂满地层与化石的墙前，用粉笔把一条从鱼到四足动物的箭头连起来
scene: 博物馆展厅里，一位学者沿着化石墙把鱼鳍到前肢的骨骼一一对应起来。 The evolutionist traced each bone from fin to limb and argued that the two forms were related.
sceneCN: 这里 evolutionist 指「进化论者」（第 1 个义项：接受或主张生物进化论的人）；句意：这位进化论者把每块骨头从鳍到肢一一对应，论证两种形态具有亲缘关系。图中可辨识物件：化石墙、鱼鳍骨骼、前肢骨骼、粉笔箭头。

pos.zh: 进化论者；支持进化论的人（可数，复数为 evolutionists）
进化论的（作定语，如 evolutionist view）

senses.title: A supporter of biological evolution
senses.definition: a person who accepts the theory that species change through descent with modification
senses.definitionCN: 接受物种经由共同祖先与变异而演变这一理论的人
senses.example: As a convinced evolutionist, she treated the fossil series as evidence of descent.
senses.exampleCN: 作为坚定的进化论者，她把这一化石序列视为共同祖先的证据。
senses.why: -ist marks a person who holds a doctrine, so evolutionist names the holder of the evolution doctrine.
senses.whyCN: -ist 标记持某种学说的人，因此 evolutionist 指进化论这一学说的持有者。

senses.title: A scientist who studies evolution
senses.definition: a researcher whose professional work is the study of evolutionary processes
senses.definitionCN: 以研究进化过程为专业工作的研究者
senses.example: The evolutionist compared fin bones across three lineages.
senses.exampleCN: 这位进化研究者比较了三个谱系的鳍骨。
senses.why: the label can shift from belief to profession, naming the person who works on the process rather than merely accepting it.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签可从信念转到职业，指实际研究该过程的人，而不只是接受该理论的人。

senses.title: A social evolutionist
senses.titleCN: 社会进化论者：把进化观用于社会
senses.definition: a person who applies evolutionary ideas to the development of societies
senses.definitionCN: 把进化观念用于社会发展的论者
senses.example: Nineteenth-century social evolutionists ranked societies on a single ladder.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪的社会进化论者把社会排在同一条阶梯上。
senses.why: the suffix travels to other fields, so the word can name someone applying selection and progress language to culture.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀可迁移到其他领域，因此该词也指把选择与进步话语用于文化的人。

senses.title: Attributive use: evolutionist thinking
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：进化论的（观点、论证）
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean 'of or belonging to the evolutionist position'
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示「属于进化论立场的」
senses.example: The paper reviewed the evolutionist argument without endorsing it.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文评述了进化论论证，但并未为其背书。
senses.why: English lets an agent noun work as a modifier, so the person label becomes an adjective of stance.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许施动名词作修饰语，于是指人的标签变成表立场的定语。

senses.title: The opposing label in a debate
senses.titleCN: 论战中的对举标签：与神创论者相对
senses.definition: a term used for one side in public disputes over creation and evolution
senses.definitionCN: 在关于创造与进化的公共争论中指其中一方
senses.example: In the 1925 trial the evolutionist and the creationist were pitted against each other.
senses.exampleCN: 1925 年的那场审判里，进化论者与神创论者被摆在对立面。
senses.why: labels harden when a debate has two sides, so the word becomes a team name as much as a description.
senses.whyCN: 当争论分成两方，标签就会硬化，于是这个词既是描述，也是阵营名。

senses.title: One who applies evolutionary thinking elsewhere
senses.titleCN: 跨领域应用者：把进化思维用于别处
senses.definition: a person who extends evolutionary reasoning to language, technology or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 把进化推理扩展到语言、技术或行为的人
senses.example: An evolutionist of language studies how words survive in use.
senses.exampleCN: 语言进化论者研究词语如何在使用中存活。
senses.why: once the mechanism is abstracted from biology, its advocates in other fields also carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦机制从生物学中抽象出来，其他领域的倡导者也带上这个名称。

senses.title: A historical label for pre-Darwinian transformists
senses.titleCN: 历史标签：达尔文之前的转变论者
senses.definition: a term used for earlier thinkers who held that species change, before Darwin's mechanism
senses.definitionCN: 指在达尔文机制之前就主张物种会变化的早期思想家
senses.example: Lamarck is often called an evolutionist avant la lettre.
senses.exampleCN: 拉马克常被称为「尚未有该词之时的进化论者」。
senses.why: historians apply a later label backwards, so the word can name thinkers who lacked the mechanism but held the change.
senses.whyCN: 史学家把后来的标签回溯使用，因此该词可指没有机制、但主张变化的思想家。

senses.title: A loose or pejorative use
senses.titleCN: 泛称或贬义：被对手当作贬号
senses.definition: a loose label for anyone seen as pushing evolutionary ideas too far
senses.definitionCN: 对任何被认为过度推行进化观念者的泛称或贬称
senses.example: The critic dismissed the plan as the work of evolutionists.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者轻蔑地把该方案说成进化论者的产物。
senses.why: an -ist label can be used to dismiss, so the word sometimes says more about the speaker than the person named.
senses.whyCN: -ist 标签可用于贬斥，因此这个词有时更多反映说话者，而非被指者。

intro.en: Evolutionist joins evolution, from Latin evolutio 'an unrolling', to the agent suffix -ist. The word is a nineteenth-century formation, and dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: evolutionist 由出自拉丁 evolutio「展开」的 evolution 加施动后缀 -ist 构成，是 19 世纪的造词，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Volvere meant 'to roll, turn'; its compounds include revolvere 'to roll back' and involvere 'to wrap up'.
items.cn: volvere 意为「滚动、转动」，其复合词包括 revolvere「卷回」与 involvere「包卷」。

items.en: E- 'out' plus volvere gave evolvere 'to roll out, unroll', as when a scroll is opened.
items.cn: e-「向外」加 volvere 得 evolvere「展开、铺开」，如展开一卷书。

items.en: Evolutio named the act of unrolling; English evolution first meant the unfolding of a plan or a book.
items.cn: evolutio 指展开的动作；英语 evolution 最初指计划或书卷的展开。

items.en: By the early nineteenth century evolution was used for the gradual development of species, and Darwin fixed the modern sense in 1859.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪初，evolution 已用于指物种的逐步发展，达尔文于 1859 年确定了现代含义。

items.en: The agent noun evolutionist appears in the early nineteenth century for those who held that species change.
items.cn: 施动名词 evolutionist 出现于 19 世纪初，指主张物种会变化的人。

items.en: The exact first citation of evolutionist is uncertain, and its shift from belief to profession is not dated to a single text.
items.cn: evolutionist 的确切最早书证不确定；它从信念转为职业的转变也无法归到某一文本。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same volvere family; group two holds labels for people on either side of the debate.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 volvere 词族的形近词；第二组是争论双方的人物标签。

entries.definition: The unfolding or change of a lineage. Evolutionist names a person who accepts or studies it.
entries.definitionCN: 指谱系的展开或变化；evolutionist 指接受或研究它的人。

entries.definition: Relating to evolution, as in evolutionary biology. It describes ideas or processes, not a holder of them.
entries.definitionCN: 指与进化相关的，如进化生物学；描述观念或过程，而非持有者。

entries.definition: The system of belief that evolution explains change, sometimes extended to society. Evolutionist is the person who holds it.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为进化能解释变化的信念体系，有时扩展到社会；evolutionist 是持有该体系的人。

entries.definition: To develop gradually. It can be used of species, plans or opinions, without any person label.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐步发展，可用于物种、计划或观点，不含人物标签。

entries.definition: One who accepts Darwin's specific mechanism of natural selection. All Darwinists are evolutionists, but not all evolutionists are Darwinists.
entries.definitionCN: 指接受达尔文具体自然选择机制的人；达尔文主义者都是进化论者，反之不然。

entries.definition: One who holds that life was created directly rather than descended. It is the usual counterpart in public debate.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为生命被直接创造而非演化而来的人，是公共争论中常见的对立标签。

entries.definition: An older word for one who holds that species transform over time, used before evolution became standard.
entries.definitionCN: 指主张物种随时间转变的较早用词，在 evolution 成为标准说法之前使用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: evolution 'unrolling' + -ist 'one who holds': one who holds the unrolling view of life.
normal.cn: evolution「展开」+ -ist「持有者」：持有生命展开观的人。

normal.en: The family runs evolve, evolution, evolutionary, evolutionism, evolutionist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evolve、evolution、evolutionary、evolutionism、evolutionist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: convinced evolutionist, social evolutionist, evolutionist argument.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：坚定的进化论者、社会进化论者、进化论论证。

normal.en: Pair it with Darwinist: the wider label versus the narrower one.
normal.cn: 把它与 Darwinist 配对：一个更宽，一个更窄。

normal.en: Pair it with creationist: the two sides of the same public argument.
normal.cn: 把它与 creationist 配对：同一场公共争论的两方。

abstract.en: Picture a scholar joining fin bones to limb bones with chalk lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一位学者用粉笔把鳍骨与肢骨连成线。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree drawn over a wall of fossils.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅画在化石墙上的家族树。

abstract.en: Picture two debaters on a stage, each with a fixed label.
abstract.cn: 想象台上两位辩手，各自带着固定标签。

examples.en: The evolutionist argued that the shared bones implied shared ancestry.
examples.cn: 这位进化论者论证共有骨骼意味着共同祖先。

examples.en: Social evolutionists of the nineteenth century often ranked cultures in a single line.
examples.cn: 19 世纪的社会进化论者常把各种文化排成一条单线。

examples.en: The court case turned evolutionists and creationists into public camps.
examples.cn: 那场官司把进化论者与神创论者变成了公开的阵营。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「进化（evolution）+ 人（-ist）」——相信生命是一卷慢慢展开的画轴的人 → 进化论者

root: 拉丁 e-「向外」+ volvere「滚动」→ evolvere「展开」→ evolutio「展开」；英语 evolution 先指书卷或计划的展开，19 世纪转指物种演变，加 -ist 构成 evolutionist。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a believer to a researcher, then to social and attributive uses, a debate camp, a cross-field label, a historical label and finally a dismissal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从信众到研究者，再到社会用法与定语用法、争论阵营、跨领域标签、历史标签，最后落到贬称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scholar drawing a line from a fin bone to a limb bone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位学者把鳍骨与肢骨连成一线。

branches.en: BELIEF AND WORK: the same label covers those who accept the theory and those who study it.
branches.cn: 信念与工作：同一标签既指接受理论者，也指研究理论者。

branches.en: EXTENSION: the label travels to society, language and technology.
branches.cn: 外延：标签迁移到社会、语言与技术。

branches.en: MODIFIER: the person word becomes a stance adjective.
branches.cn: 修饰语：指人名词转为表立场的定语。

branches.en: CAMPS: in debate the label hardens into a team name or an insult.
branches.cn: 阵营：在争论中标签硬化为队名或贬称。

branches.en: HINDSIGHT: historians apply the later label to earlier thinkers.
branches.cn: 回溯：史学家把后来的标签用于更早的思想家。

intro.en: The noun is evolution plus the agent suffix -ist; evolution itself is a Latin-derived noun in -ion from evolvere.
intro.cn: 这个名词是 evolution 加施动后缀 -ist；evolution 本身是由 evolvere 派生的带 -ion 拉丁来源名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere and evolvere yield evolve, evolution, evolutionary, evolutionism, evolutionist and involve, revolve, volume.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 volvere 与 evolvere 衍生 evolve、evolution、evolutionary、evolutionism、evolutionist，以及 involve、revolve、volume。

items.meaning: one who holds or studies evolution
items.meaningCN: 持有或研究进化论的人
items.example: The evolutionist compared three fossil series.
items.exampleCN: 这位进化论者比较了三个化石序列。

items.example: The evolution of the eye is a classic case.
items.exampleCN: 眼睛的进化是经典案例。

items.example: An evolutionary tree links the lineages.
items.exampleCN: 一棵进化树把各谱系连起来。

items.meaning: the doctrine that evolution explains change
items.meaningCN: 认为进化能解释变化的学说
items.exampleCN: 社会进化主义塑造了维多利亚时代的人类学。

items.example: The book took an evolutionistic line.
items.exampleCN: 这本书采取进化论的立场。

items.example: The fin evolved into a limb.
The survey involved three field seasons.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查涉及三个野外季节。

items.meaning: to roll back; to go round
items.example: The debate revolved around one fossil.
items.exampleCN: 争论围绕一块化石打转。

definition_zh: n. 充电器；（古）战马
definition_en: a device that puts electricity into a battery; an old word for a war horse
core_image: 插头接上墙，指示灯变红
scene: 手机没电了，他从包里翻出充电器。 His phone died, so he dug the charger out of his bag.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：charger 指充电器；句意是手机没电，他从包里翻出充电器。

pos.zh: 充电器；战马

senses.title: The power device
senses.definition: a device that supplies electricity to recharge a battery
senses.definitionCN: 给电池充电的供电装置
senses.example: The charger is still in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 充电器还在车里。
senses.why: The device charges a battery in the old sense of loading it.
senses.whyCN: 这个装置按 charge 古老的「装填」义给电池装载电量。

senses.title: A war horse
senses.definition: an old word for a horse ridden into battle
senses.definitionCN: 指载人上阵的战马的旧词
senses.example: The knight calmed his charger.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士安抚他的战马。
senses.why: A charger carried a rider loaded for war.
senses.whyCN: 战马载着全副武装的骑手。

intro.en: Charger is charge plus -er; charge itself came from a Latin verb for loading a cart.
intro.cn: charger 是 charge 加 -er；charge 本身来自拉丁语「装车」的动词。

items.en: Carricare means to load a cart.
items.cn: carricare 意为装车。

items.en: Chargier means to load or burden.
items.cn: chargier 意为装载或使负担。

items.en: Charge means to load or entrust.
items.cn: 十三世纪 charge 意为装载或委托。

items.en: A charger is a horse for battle.
items.cn: 十六世纪指战马。

items.en: Charge comes to mean storing electric energy.
items.cn: 十九世纪转为储存电能。

items.en: A charger refills a battery.
items.cn: 二十世纪指给电池补充电量的装置。

note.en: The look-alike group bends the ending; the near-meaning group lists power accessories.
note.cn: 形近组改动词尾；近义组列出供电配件。

entries.definition: To load or to bill.
entries.definitionCN: 装载；收费。

entries.definition: A hired contract.
entries.definitionCN: 包租契约。

entries.definition: Something that changes things.
entries.definitionCN: 改变者。

entries.definition: A device joining two fittings.
entries.definitionCN: 适配器。

entries.definition: A base that powers a device.
entries.definitionCN: 扩展坞。

entries.definition: A wire carrying current.
entries.definitionCN: 电缆。

normalIntro.en: A charger loads a battery the way a horse once carried a rider.
normalIntro.cn: 充电器给电池装电，就像战马当年载人。

normal.en: Carricare means to load a cart.
normal.cn: carricare 意为装车。

normal.en: Charge means to load something up.
normal.cn: charge 意为装载。

normal.en: A war horse carried a loaded rider.
normal.cn: 战马载着全副武装的骑手。

normal.en: A battery is loaded with power.
normal.cn: 电池被装上电量。

normal.en: The thing that loads it is a charger.
normal.cn: 给电池装载的东西就是充电器。

abstract.en: A cable feeding a small hunger.
abstract.cn: 一根喂饱小小饥渴的线。

abstract.en: A red light promising energy.
abstract.cn: 一盏承诺能量的红灯。

abstract.en: Loading, old and new.
abstract.cn: 古老与崭新的装载。

examples.en: Leave the charger plugged in overnight.
examples.cn: 把充电器插着过夜。

examples.en: This charger fits three phone models.
examples.cn: 这个充电器适配三款手机。

examples.en: A charger must match the battery voltage.
examples.cn: 充电器必须与电池电压匹配。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「插着」——插着电，就是充电器。

root: 拉丁语 carricare（装车）→ 古法语 chargier → charge → charger

sensesIntro.en: The battery device and the battle horse both come from a word for loading.
sensesIntro.cn: 给电池充电的装置与战马，都出自「装载」一词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cable running from a wall socket to a red light
core.cn: 核心意象：从墙插连到红灯的一条线

branches.en: A cable snaking from a wall socket.
branches.cn: 从墙插蜿蜒而出的线。

branches.en: A red light turning green.
branches.cn: 由红转绿的指示灯。

branches.en: A horse stamping before battle.
branches.cn: 战前跺脚的马。

branches.en: Armour strapped to a saddle.
branches.cn: 绑在马鞍上的甲胄。

branches.en: Something loaded up, with power or with a rider.
branches.cn: 装满电或载着骑手的某物。

intro.en: Charger is a native suffix on a French verb; the list below adds words of loading and carrying.
intro.cn: charger 是法语动词加英语本族词缀；下面列出装载与携带词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin carricare is to load, carrus is a cart and portare is to carry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carricare 意为装载，carrus 意为车，portare 意为携带。

latinEntries.exampleCN: carricare 产生 charge 与 cargo。
carrus 产生 car 与 carriage。
battuere 产生 battery 与 battle。

definition_zh: n. 黄水仙；水仙黄；春天与威尔士的象征
definition_en: a spring bulb with a yellow trumpet-shaped flower, its colour, or an emblem of Wales and spring
core_image: 三月山坡上一片明黄的小喇叭，齐齐朝着太阳抬头
scene: 三月的山坡上开满了黄水仙。 The hillside was covered with daffodils in March.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：daffodil 指黄水仙这种花；句意是三月山坡上开满了黄水仙。

pos.zh: 黄水仙；水仙黄；春天与威尔士的象征

senses.title: Yellow flower
senses.definition: a spring plant with a yellow trumpet rising from a bulb
senses.definitionCN: 春天从鳞茎抽出黄色喇叭状花冠的植物
senses.example: Daffodils are the first sign of spring.
senses.exampleCN: 黄水仙是春天最早的信号。
senses.why: A field of small yellow trumpets.
senses.whyCN: 一片明黄的小喇叭。

senses.title: Bright yellow
senses.definition: the clear warm yellow of this flower
senses.definitionCN: 这种花明亮温暖的黄色
senses.example: She painted the door daffodil yellow.
senses.exampleCN: 她把门漆成水仙黄。
senses.why: A pot of warm yellow paint.
senses.whyCN: 一罐暖黄色的颜料。

senses.title: National emblem
senses.definition: the flower worn in Wales on the day of its patron saint
senses.definitionCN: 在威尔士守护神纪念日佩戴的花

senses.exampleCN: 人们在三月一日佩戴黄水仙。
senses.why: A yellow flower pinned to a coat.
senses.whyCN: 一枚别在外套上的黄花。

intro.en: Daffodil grew from asphodel, with the Dutch article de fused onto the front.
intro.cn: daffodil 由 asphodel 演变而来，荷兰语冠词 de 被粘在了词首。

items.en: Asphodelos named a meadow flower of the dead.
items.cn: asphodelos 指冥界草地上的一种花。

items.en: Asphodelus carried the name into herbals.
items.cn: asphodelus 把这个名字带进草药志。

items.en: Affodillus was the shortened medieval form.
items.cn: affodillus 是中世纪的缩略形式。

items.en: De affodil meant the affodil, with an article.
items.cn: de affodil 意为「那株水仙」，带着冠词。

items.en: Daffodil absorbed the article into the word.
items.cn: 十六世纪 daffodil 把冠词吸收进词里。

items.en: The daffodil became a Welsh national emblem.
items.cn: 十九世纪黄水仙成为威尔士的民族标志。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the old asphodel shape; the near-meaning group names other spring bulbs.

entries.definition: A lily-like flower of old poetry.
entries.definitionCN: 日光兰；旧诗中的冥界花。

entries.definition: An old spelling of daffodil.
entries.definitionCN: daffodil 的旧拼法。

entries.definition: Slightly crazy or foolish.

entries.definition: The plant genus that includes daffodils.

entries.definition: A spring bulb with cup-shaped flowers.
entries.definitionCN: 郁金香。

entries.definition: A small early spring flower.
entries.definitionCN: 番红花。

entries.definition: A narcissus with small scented flowers.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小花香浓的水仙。

normalIntro.en: Daffodil hides de affodil: the article stuck to the flower.
normalIntro.cn: daffodil 里藏着 de affodil：冠词粘在了花名上。

normal.en: Asphodel was a flower of the dead.
normal.cn: asphodel 是冥界的花。

normal.en: Affodil shortened that long name.
normal.cn: affodil 把那个长名字缩短了。

normal.en: Dutch de means the.
normal.cn: 荷兰语 de 相当于「那个」。

normal.en: De affodil became daffodil.
normal.cn: de affodil 连读成了 daffodil。

normal.en: A daffodil is a yellow trumpet.
normal.cn: 黄水仙是一支黄色小喇叭。
