definition_zh: 缓冲物；缓冲区；缓冲者；减震垫
definition_en: something or someone that lessens the shock of impact between two forces or systems
core_image: 两个硬物之间的软垫，把撞击吸掉
scene: 邻里纠纷越闹越大，居委会大叔夹在中间两边劝。 The community worker acted as a buffer between the angry neighbors.
sceneCN: 这里 buffer 是「缓冲者、调和人」（第 3 个义项：在人或群体间缓解冲突）；句意是社区工作者在怒气冲冲的邻居之间充当缓冲。

pos.zh: 缓冲物；缓冲区；缓冲者；减震垫
缓冲；减轻冲击；保护

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「缓冲过程」（如视频加载）
buffer 的同族词，义为「软皮；柔光革」，由此引申「爱好者」
形近词，义为「打击；自助餐」，词源不同

senses.title: A shock-absorbing pad or device
senses.definition: a device or material that absorbs shock between colliding objects
senses.definitionCN: 吸收碰撞冲击的装置或材料
senses.example: Rubber buffers protect the docked boats.
senses.exampleCN: 橡胶缓冲垫保护着停靠的船只。
senses.why: The root sense is to buff, to polish or soften; a soft thing takes the blow.
senses.whyCN: 词根义为打磨、使柔软；柔软之物承担了撞击。

senses.title: A neutral zone or reserve
senses.definition: a neutral area or spare reserve that separates or protects against interference
senses.definitionCN: 隔开势力或抵御波动的中立地带或备用储备
senses.example: The treaty created a buffer zone along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 条约沿边界设立了缓冲区。
senses.why: A physical cushion generalizes into any spacing that keeps two systems from clashing.
senses.whyCN: 实物软垫推广为一切「隔开以免相撞」的空间或储备。

senses.title: A person or thing that shields
senses.definition: a person or thing that protects someone from harm, criticism or unpleasantness
senses.definitionCN: 使人免受伤害、批评或不快的保护者
senses.example: An assistant can buffer the director from daily complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 助理可以为主任挡下日常抱怨。
senses.why: Anything that stands between pressure and its target becomes a cushion.
senses.whyCN: 凡挡在压力与承受者之间的东西都在起软垫作用，义项由物及人。

senses.title: To lessen an impact
senses.definition: to reduce the harmful effect of something by acting as a cushion
senses.definitionCN: 像软垫一样减轻冲击或不良影响
senses.example: Savings buffered the family against the income drop.
senses.exampleCN: 积蓄缓冲了这个家庭的收入骤降。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to provide buffering is to buffer.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，「起缓冲作用」即「缓冲」。

intro.en: Buffer grew from the verb buff, whose origin is imitative of soft blows.
intro.cn: buffer 由动词 buff 滋生而来，buff 的来源一般认为是对软性击打声的拟声。

items.en: buff arose in late Middle English, probably echoing the sound of soft puffs and blows.
items.cn: buff 出现于中古英语晚期，一般认为是拟声词，摹仿噗噗的软击声。

items.en: to buff meant to strike, then to polish with soft leather.
items.cn: buff 先指击打，后指用软皮抛光。

items.en: buffer named the polishing wheel, then the padded bumper on carriages.
items.cn: buffer 先指抛光轮，后指车厢上的软垫挡块。

items.en: railways and diplomacy adopted buffer for shock-absorbing zones and states.
items.cn: 铁路与外交领域借用 buffer 指减震装置与缓冲地带。

items.en: computing added the data buffer; the word now spans machines, people and memory.
items.cn: 计算机领域又添「数据缓冲区」，该词现遍及机械、人际与存储。

note.en: Buffer sits among buff- spellings of soft striking and beside words for protective spacing.
note.cn: buffer 处于表软击的 buff- 词形群中，并与表防护间隔的词为邻。

entries.definition: to polish; bare skin; an enthusiast
entries.definitionCN: 抛光；裸露的；爱好者，buffer 的词根

entries.definition: a meal laid out; repeated blows
entries.definitionCN: 自助餐；（复数）打击，拼形相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a wild ox; to bewilder
entries.definitionCN: 水牛；使困惑，仅开头字母相同

entries.definition: protected by a buffer
entries.definitionCN: buffer 的过去分词，受缓冲保护的

entries.definition: a soft pad; to soften impact
entries.definitionCN: 软垫；缓和冲击

entries.definition: a device that damps jolts
entries.definitionCN: 减震器

entries.definition: one who stands between parties
entries.definitionCN: 中间人，调解者

entries.definition: a thing that blocks passage
entries.definitionCN: 屏障，阻断而非缓冲的对照

entries.definition: a measure giving protection
entries.definitionCN: 保障措施，防护手段

normalIntro.en: Buff the surface soft, and the blow lands nowhere hard.
normalIntro.cn: 把表面打磨柔软，冲击便无处着力。

normal.en: The root buff means to soften by polishing.
normal.cn: 词根 buff 意为抛光使之柔。

normal.en: Film buffs know buffering from slow video.
normal.cn: 影迷从卡顿的视频里熟知 buffering。

normal.en: A buffer zone keeps armies apart.
normal.cn: 缓冲区把军队隔开。

normal.en: Buffer state is the classic diplomatic term.
normal.cn: 缓冲国是经典外交术语。

normal.en: The verb buffer takes the blow itself.
normal.cn: 动词 buffer 表示自己承受冲击。

abstract.en: Feel a pillow swallow the blow meant for you.
abstract.cn: 感受一只枕头替你吞下本该落在你身上的重击。

abstract.en: See a green belt of park separating two roads.
abstract.cn: 看见一条绿带隔开两条大路。

abstract.en: Hear a video pause as the buffer fills.
abstract.cn: 听视频在缓冲加载时停顿。

examples.en: The diplomat served as a buffer during the tense talks.
examples.cn: 谈判剑拔弩张之际，这位外交官起了缓冲作用。

examples.en: Trees buffer the house from highway noise.
examples.cn: 树木为房子挡住了公路噪音。

examples.en: Emergency funds buffer schools against budget cuts.
examples.cn: 应急基金缓冲了预算削减对学校的冲击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「巴佛」——像佛一样温和的「巴」掌垫，打过来也不疼，缓冲减震全靠它。

root: buffer 由动词 buff（拟声词，摹仿软性击打声，后义为用软皮抛光）加名词后缀 -er 构成，指「起打磨、软化作用之物」，再由抛光轮引申到减震垫、缓冲区，词源无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: A soft pad that takes blows widens into protective zones, human intermediaries, and finally the verb of cushioning.
sensesIntro.cn: 承受撞击的软垫，先扩展为防护地带与居间之人，最终凝为「缓冲」这一动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft pad swallowing the blow between two hard things.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块软垫在两个硬物之间吞下撞击。

branches.en: buffers on a train carriage
branches.cn: 火车车厢的缓冲器

branches.en: trees that buffer the wind
branches.cn: 为风起缓冲作用的树木

branches.en: a demilitarized buffer zone
branches.cn: 非军事缓冲区

branches.en: a secretary as buffer
branches.cn: 充当缓冲的秘书

branches.en: buffer stocks against famine
branches.cn: 抵御饥荒的缓冲储备

intro.en: Buffer is an agent noun: the verb buff plus -er, the doer or tool.
intro.cn: buffer 是施动名词：动词 buff 加后缀 -er，表「起作用者或工具」。

latinIntro.en: The root is imitative English; Latin offers no ancestor here.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是英语拟声词，拉丁语中并无其祖先。

items.meaning: one that does or a tool that does

definition_zh: 合法的；合理的；正当的；正统的；婚生的
definition_en: allowed by law, supported by good reason, genuine and valid, or rightful by established authority
core_image: 市政厅窗口前，办事员把执照递到申请人手上，逐条核对经营范围和地址
scene: 市政厅窗口前，办事员把执照递到申请人手上，逐条核对经营范围和地址。 Only businesses with a legitimate licence may operate here.
sceneCN: 这里指依法获准的（第 1 个义项：合法的）；句意为只有持有合法执照的企业才能在此经营。

pos.zh: 合法的；合理的；正当的；正统的；婚生的
使合法；使正当（较少用）

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「合法性；正当性」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词尾构成，义为「合法地；正当地」
由该形容词加表示「使成为」的动词尾构成，义为「使合法化」
由同族动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「合法化；认领」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「非法的；不正当的」

senses.title: Allowed by law
senses.definition: permitted by the legal order of a country or institution
senses.definitionCN: 为一个国家或机构的法律秩序所允许
senses.example: Only a legitimate licence allows you to trade here.
senses.exampleCN: 只有合法执照才允许你在此经营。
senses.why: The Latin root is law itself, so the first sense is simply conformity with what the law permits.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根就是「法律」，所以第一个义项就是与法律所允许的一致。

senses.title: Supported by good reason
senses.definition: justified by evidence or by a fair argument, even where no law is involved
senses.definitionCN: 由证据或公平论证证明为正当，即使不涉及法律
senses.example: Parents have a legitimate concern about the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 家长对新课表有合理的关切。
senses.why: Law is the model of what is acceptable, and the word extends to whatever would pass a fair test of reason.
senses.whyCN: 法律是「可接受」的范本，这个词于是扩展到任何能通过公正理性检验的事物。

senses.title: Genuine and valid
senses.definition: of a document, claim or result that is authentic and stands up to checking
senses.definitionCN: 指文件、主张或结果真实且经得起核查
senses.example: The archive held a legitimate copy of the original map.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆藏有一份真实有效的原图副本。
senses.why: A forged document is illegitimate even when no statute is named, because authenticity is a kind of law.
senses.whyCN: 伪造文件即使不涉及具体法条也是不正当的，因为真实性本身是一种法则。

senses.title: Born to married parents
senses.definition: in older legal language, of a child born within a recognized marriage
senses.definitionCN: 旧法律用语中指在获认可的婚姻中出生的孩子
senses.example: The old will named only the legitimate son as heir.
senses.exampleCN: 那份旧遗嘱只指定婚生儿子为继承人。
senses.why: Marriage was once the legal form that made a birth regular, so the word applied to the child as well as the union.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻曾是使出生合乎规范的法定形式，因此这个词既用于婚姻，也用于孩子。

senses.title: Rightful by established authority
senses.definition: of a ruler or government whose right to rule is accepted rather than merely seized
senses.definitionCN: 指统治者或政府的统治权被承认，而不只是被夺取
senses.example: The old dynasty was still regarded as the legitimate ruler of the province.
senses.exampleCN: 旧王朝仍被视为该省的合法统治者。
senses.why: Power becomes authority when it can point to a recognized line, and the word names that recognized line.
senses.whyCN: 权力在能指向一条被承认的谱系时成为权威，而这个词命名的正是那条被承认的谱系。

senses.title: Of lawful business activity
senses.definition: of trade, work or profit that is registered, taxed and open to inspection
senses.definitionCN: 指登记、纳税并接受检查的贸易、工作或收益
senses.example: The family ran a legitimate shipping business for three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人合法经营航运生意达三代之久。
senses.why: Commerce needed a word to separate licensed trade from smuggling, and the legal sense did the work.
senses.whyCN: 商业需要一个词把持牌贸易与走私区分开，而「合法」这一义项正好承担了这个功能。

senses.title: Of a fair question or worry
senses.definition: of a doubt or objection that deserves an answer rather than dismissal
senses.definitionCN: 指值得回答而不该被驳回的怀疑或反对
senses.example: It is legitimate to ask where the money went.
senses.exampleCN: 追问这笔钱去了哪里是合理的。
senses.why: A question is legitimate when it has a right to be heard, and rights are the shadow of law behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题在有权被听见时就是合理的，而权利正是这个词背后法律的影子。

senses.title: Of a government with accepted title
senses.titleCN: 具有被承认资格的正统政府
senses.definition: of a regime recognized by its own people or by other states as properly constituted
senses.definitionCN: 指被本国人民或其他国家承认其组建正当的政权
senses.example: Foreign offices argued over which cabinet was legitimate.
senses.exampleCN: 各国外交部门争论哪一个内阁才是正统的。
senses.why: Recognition is the international form of law, and a government without it is called illegitimate even if it holds the capital.
senses.whyCN: 承认是法律在国际层面的形式，缺少承认的政府即使占据首都也被称为不正当。

senses.title: Of a claim one is entitled to make
senses.definition: of a demand that rests on a right rather than on force or favour
senses.definitionCN: 指依据权利而非武力或恩惠提出的要求
senses.example: The workers had a legitimate claim to the unpaid wages.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们对未付工资有正当的主张权。
senses.why: A claim is legitimate when it can be traced to an entitlement, which is again law in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 主张在能追溯到一项权利时就是正当的，这又是微缩的法律。

intro.en: Legitimate comes from Latin legitimatus, the past participle of legitimare, to make lawful, from legitimus, lawful, from lex, law.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 legitimatus，即 legitimare「使合法」的过去分词，而 legitimare 出自 legitimus「合法的」，其根为 lex「法律」。

items.en: Lex meant law or statute, and its stem legis appears in legal, legislate and legitimacy alike.
items.cn: lex 意为法律或法令，其词干 legis 同时出现在 legal、legislate 与 legitimacy 中。

items.en: The adjective meant lawful or according to law, and it could describe a person, a claim or a birth.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为合法的或依法的，可形容人、主张或出生。

items.en: The verb meant to make lawful or to declare lawful, used of wills, marriages and offices.
items.cn: 这个动词意为使合法或宣布合法，曾用于遗嘱、婚姻与职位。

items.en: French carried the adjective to English, which kept the legal core while widening it to reason and authenticity.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词带给英语，英语保留法律核心，同时把它拓宽到理性与真实性。

items.en: English used the word for lawful births and lawful rulers before it used it for fair arguments; the date of the widening is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语先用它讲婚生与合法统治者，之后才用它讲公正论证；这一拓宽的年代不确定。

items.en: Today the word often means simply reasonable, as in a legitimate question, with the legal sense still underneath.
items.cn: 今天这个词常只表示「合理」，如「合理的疑问」，但法律义仍在底下。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like legitimate; the second group names neighbouring ideas of law and fairness.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 legitimate 相近；第二组是与「法律、公正」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The quality of being lawful or accepted as rightful.
entries.definitionCN: 指合法或被承认为正当的性质。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a lawful or justified way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以合法或有正当理由的方式。

entries.definition: To make something lawful or acceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事物合法或可接受。

entries.definition: To make laws; it shares the law root but is not formed from legitimate.
entries.definitionCN: 指制定法律；共享法律词根，但并非由本词派生。

entries.definition: Property left by will; it looks close but comes from a word for a commission or bequest.
entries.definitionCN: 指遗嘱留下的财产；形近，但来自意为「委托、遗赠」的词。

entries.definition: Permitted by statute, the plainest member of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 指为成文法所允许，是这组词中最朴素的。

entries.definition: Relating to law or allowed by it, often used of procedures.
entries.definitionCN: 指与法律有关或为法律所允许，常指程序。

entries.definition: Officially acceptable because the required conditions are met.
entries.definitionCN: 指因满足所需条件而获正式接受。

entries.definition: Shown to have a good reason behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被证明背后有充分理由。

entries.definition: Holding a position or property by proper title.
entries.definitionCN: 指凭正当名分持有职位或财产。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the law root, the three layers of the word and the phrases that keep them apart.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用「法律」词根、这个词的三层意思，以及区分这三层的搭配。

normal.en: The root is lex, law, so legitimate starts from what the law allows and then widens to what reason allows.
normal.cn: 词根意为「法律」，所以这个词从「法律允许」出发，再扩展到「理性允许」。

normal.en: Legislate and legal share the root but are different words, not derivatives of legitimate.
normal.cn: 表示「立法」与「法律的」同族词共享词根，却是另外的词，不是本词的派生词。

normal.en: A legitimate licence is lawful, a legitimate question is reasonable, a legitimate king is rightful.
normal.cn: 合法的执照、合理的疑问、正统的国王，三层意思各自清楚。

normal.en: The noun legitimacy is the abstract form used in politics and in arguments about proof.
normal.cn: 名词形式是用于政治与证据争论的抽象说法。

normal.en: Illegitimate simply adds the negative prefix and denies all three layers at once.
normal.cn: 否定形式只是加上否定前缀，一次否定三层意思。

abstract.en: Legitimacy is the story power tells about why it should be obeyed.
abstract.cn: 正当性是权力讲述的、关于自己为何该被服从的故事。

abstract.en: The word quietly moves from statutes to feelings, because people want their worries to have standing.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄悄从法条移到感受，因为人希望自己的担忧拥有地位。

abstract.en: To call something legitimate is to say it has a right to exist, not merely a permission.
abstract.cn: 称某事正当，是说它有存在的权利，而不只是有许可。

examples.en: The commission asked whether the election had produced a legitimate government.
examples.cn: 委员会询问这场选举是否产生了正统政府。

examples.en: There is a legitimate reason to delay the launch until the tests finish.
examples.cn: 把发布推迟到测试结束是有正当理由的。

examples.en: Only legitimate copies carry the printer's mark on the last page.
examples.cn: 只有正版副本的末页才带印刷商标记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「利己提马特」——凡事「利己」又「提」得出「马」上能查的凭据，才算合法正当

root: 拉丁语 legitimatus（legitimare「使合法」的过去分词）← legitimus「合法的」← lex, legis「法律」。同根有 legal、legislate、legitimacy；legacy 形近但来自「遗赠」义，不同源。三层义（合法、合理、正统）由法律义向外扩展；扩展年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses arrange three layers: law (licence, business, birth), reason (concern, question, claim) and recognized title (ruler, government, authentic document).
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项排成三层：法律（执照、经营、婚生）、理性（关切、疑问、主张）与被承认的名分（统治者、政府、真实文件）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clerk checking a licence line by line against the register.
core.cn: 核心意象：办事员把执照逐条对照登记册。

branches.en: THE LICENSED BRANCH: what the statute allows and the trade that is registered and taxed.
branches.cn: 持牌分支：成文法允许之事，以及登记纳税的经营。

branches.en: THE REASONABLE BRANCH: a fair worry and a question that deserves an answer.
branches.cn: 合理分支：公平的担忧，以及值得回答的疑问。

branches.en: THE PROOF BRANCH: an authentic copy and a claim backed by an entitlement.
branches.cn: 凭据分支：真实副本，以及有权利支撑的主张。

branches.en: THE BIRTH BRANCH: the old legal sense of a child born within marriage.
branches.cn: 出生分支：婚内所生子女的旧法律义。

branches.en: THE TITLE BRANCH: a ruler and a cabinet whose right to rule is recognized.
branches.cn: 名分分支：统治权被承认的君主与内阁。

intro.en: Legitimate is a Latin law word that English widened from statutes to reason, with a productive family on both sides.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁法律词，英语把它从法条拓宽到理性，两侧都有一族能产的派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex and its stem legis supply the root; legitimus, legitimare and legitimatus supply the forms English borrowed or imitated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lex 及其词干 legis 提供词根；legitimus、legitimare 与 legitimatus 提供英语借用或仿造的形式。

items.example: The root is short but stands under a large family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根很短，却支撑着一大族词。

items.example: The stem appears in legal and legislate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在表示「法律的」与「立法」的同族词中。

items.example: It could describe a person or a claim.
Wills and marriages were its objects.
items.exampleCN: 遗嘱与婚姻曾是它的对象。

items.example: The participle is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.example: It lets the same form serve as adjective and verb.
items.exampleCN: 它让同一形式兼作形容词与动词。
它构成表示「合法性」的名词。
它构成表示「非法的」的否定形容词。

由该形容词加表示方式的副词尾构成，义为「合法地；正当地」

definition_zh: v. 使转向；使改道；转移；转用；使分心；使娱乐
definition_en: to make something change direction or use, to draw attention away, or to entertain someone
core_image: 工人在被堵住的河流旁挖出一条新河道；一根把水从一只水箱引到另一只的管子；一只手在视野边缘挥动一块亮色布；一架从大雾跑道旁侧转离开的飞机
scene: 机场广播响起，大雾把跑道盖住了。 The flight was diverted to another airport.
sceneCN: 这里 divert 是「使改航」（第 5 个义项：让交通工具改去别的目的地）；句意：航班被改航到另一座机场。图中可辨识物件：广播喇叭、雾中的跑道、侧转的飞机、另一座机场的塔台。

pos.zh: 使转向；使改道；转移；转用；使分心；使娱乐

senses.title: Change the course
senses.definition: to make a river, road or traffic follow a different route
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使河流、道路或车流走另一条路线
senses.example: They diverted the river around the site.
senses.exampleCN: 他们让河流绕过工地。
senses.why: Workers cutting a new channel beside a blocked river.
senses.whyCN: 工人在被堵住的河流旁挖出一条新河道。

senses.title: Turn to a new use
senses.definition: to send money, goods or effort to a different purpose
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把资金、物资或精力转用于别的用途
senses.example: The funds were diverted to emergency repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 资金被转用于紧急维修。
senses.why: A pipe carrying water from one tank into another.
senses.whyCN: 一根把水从一只水箱引到另一只的管子。

senses.title: Draw attention away
senses.definition: to take the mind or the eyes off something
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把心思或目光从某事上引开
senses.example: Nothing could divert her from the task.
senses.exampleCN: 什么也不能使她放下手头的工作。
senses.why: A hand waving a bright cloth at the edge of vision.
senses.whyCN: 一只手在视野边缘挥动一块亮色布。

senses.title: Give pleasure
senses.definition: to amuse someone or fill their time enjoyably
senses.definitionCN: （动词）逗某人开心、让某人愉快地打发时间
senses.example: The clown diverted the children for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 小丑逗孩子们乐了一个小时。
senses.why: A deck of cards and a chess board on a rainy afternoon.
senses.whyCN: 雨天午后的一副纸牌和一张棋盘。

senses.title: Send to another place
senses.definition: to make a vehicle go to a different destination
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让交通工具改去别的目的地
senses.example: The flight was diverted to another airport.
senses.exampleCN: 航班被改航到另一座机场。
senses.why: A plane banking away from a fogged runway.
senses.whyCN: 一架从大雾跑道旁侧转离开的飞机。

intro.en: Divert comes from Latin divertere, to turn aside, from di- plus vertere, to turn; turning the mind aside gives both distraction and amusement.
intro.cn: divert 来自拉丁语 divertere「转到一边」，由 di- 加 vertere「转」组成；把心思转开，就同时有了「使分心」与「使娱乐」。

items.en: Latin vertere means to turn.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 意为转。

items.en: Divertere means to turn aside or away.
items.cn: divertere 意为转到一边或转开。

items.en: Old French divertir carries the sense of turning away.
items.cn: 古法语 divertir 带有转开的意思。

items.en: English divert first means to turn something aside.
items.cn: 英语 divert 最初意为使某物转向一边。

items.en: The word gains the sense of entertaining the mind.
items.cn: 这个词获得「使心情愉快」的意思。

items.en: Divert is common for traffic, funds and flights.
items.cn: divert 常用于车流、资金与航班。

note.en: Divert is making something turn aside; its look-alikes share the turn root, and its neighbours name other ways of sending or pleasing.
note.cn: divert 是使某物转开；形近词共用「转」的词根，近义词则是别的送往别处或逗人开心的方式。

entries.definition: the act or route of turning aside
entries.definitionCN: 转开的行为或路线

entries.definition: of many different kinds
entries.definitionCN: 种类繁多的

entries.definition: to turn something upside down
entries.definitionCN: 把某物上下颠倒

entries.definition: to send to a different place or purpose
entries.definitionCN: 送往别处或转作别用

entries.definition: to make something change direction on impact
entries.definitionCN: 使某物在撞击时改变方向

entries.definition: to make someone smile or laugh
entries.definitionCN: 使某人微笑或发笑

dict_mnemonic.text: divert ＝ di-（分开、到一边）＋ vert（转，拉丁语 vertere）＝「转到一边」，即改道、转用；把心思转开就是「使分心」，把无聊转开就是「使娱乐」。名词 diversion 是转开的行为，也是那条绕行路。

root: 拉丁语 vertere（转）→ divertere（转到一边）→ 古法语 divertir → 英语 divert

sensesIntro.en: One turn aside in five scenes: a new river channel, water moved between tanks, a bright cloth at the edge of the eye, cards on a rainy day and a plane leaving a fogged runway.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次转开的五个场景：新挖的河道、在水箱间移动的水、眼角的一块亮布、雨天的纸牌与离开雾中跑道的飞机。

branches.en: A river or road sent along a new route.
branches.cn: 被送上新路线的河流或道路。

branches.en: Money or effort turned to another purpose.
branches.cn: 转作别的用途的资金或精力。

branches.en: Attention pulled away from the task.
branches.cn: 从任务上被拉开的注意力。

branches.en: A mind turned from boredom to pleasure.
branches.cn: 从无聊转向愉快的心情。

branches.en: Both send a moving thing to another place.
branches.cn: 两者都把移动中的东西送往别处。

intro.en: Divert is di- plus the turn root vert-; the same root builds convert, invert and reverse, and the noun diversion adds -ion.
intro.cn: divert 由 di- 加转的词根 vert- 构成；同一个词根造出 convert、invert 与 reverse，名词 diversion 再加上 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere means to turn, divertere to turn aside, and diversus turned in different ways.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 意为转，divertere 意为转到一边，diversus 意为转向不同方向的。

definition_zh: 加强；加剧；强化；增强
definition_en: to make something stronger, sharper or more concentrated, or to become so
core_image: 炉门被拉开，风箱越推越快，火苗从橙红窜成刺眼的白
scene: 谈判没有进展，双方反而把条件提得更高，气氛越来越紧。 Both sides intensify pressure as the talks stall.
sceneCN: 这里指把压力加得更强（第 2 个义项：加剧冲突或压力）；句意为谈判停滞后双方都在加大压力。图中可辨识物件：被拉开的炉门、加速的风箱、窜高的火焰。

pos.zh: 加强；加剧；强化

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「加强；加剧」
由该动词加表示施动者或工具的名词尾构成，义为「加强成分；增强剂」
由同一拉丁词干加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「强度」
由同一拉丁词干构成的形容词，义为「强烈的；紧张的」
由同一词干加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「密集的；加强的」

senses.title: To increase strength
senses.definition: to raise the strength, force or level of an action or quality
senses.definitionCN: 提高某一行动或性质的强度、力度或水平
senses.example: The crew intensified the light before the final inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后检查前，班组把照明加强了。
senses.why: The root means stretched tight, and intensifying is pulling that tension higher.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「拉紧」，加强就是把那股张力再拉高。

senses.title: To sharpen a conflict
senses.definition: to make a dispute, pressure or hostility more acute
senses.definitionCN: 使争端、压力或敌意更尖锐
senses.example: Sanctions intensified the dispute over the border.
senses.exampleCN: 制裁加剧了边境争端。
senses.why: Conflict is tension between two sides, and the verb raises the tension.
senses.whyCN: 冲突是两方之间的张力，这个动词把张力调高。

senses.title: To heighten a feeling
senses.definition: to make an emotion or sensation more vivid or harder to ignore
senses.definitionCN: 使情绪或感觉更鲜明、更难忽视
senses.example: The silence intensified the fear in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默让屋里的恐惧更强烈。
senses.why: Feelings are measured by how tightly they hold attention, so more tension means more feeling.
senses.whyCN: 情绪以攥住注意力的松紧来衡量，张力越大，感受越强。

senses.title: To step up an effort
senses.definition: to make work or a campaign more concentrated and frequent
senses.definitionCN: 使工作或运动更集中、更频繁
senses.example: Volunteers intensified the search after nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 入夜后，志愿者加紧搜寻。
senses.why: Effort has a dial, and the verb turns it up rather than changing its direction.
senses.whyCN: 努力有一个旋钮，这个动词把它拧大，而不是换方向。

senses.title: To raise scrutiny or attention
senses.definition: to make examination, attention or criticism closer and more constant
senses.definitionCN: 使审视、关注或批评更贴近、更持续
senses.example: Regulators intensified checks on the export route.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构加强了对出口路线的检查。
senses.why: Scrutiny is pressure applied to a process, and the verb says the pressure rose.
senses.whyCN: 审视是对流程施加的压力，这个动词说压力升高了。

senses.title: To strengthen an effect
senses.definition: to make the visible or audible effect of something more pronounced
senses.definitionCN: 使某物的视觉或听觉效果更明显
senses.example: The new coating intensified the contrast of the print.
senses.exampleCN: 新涂层增强了印刷的对比度。
senses.why: Effects are read by the senses, and intensifying pushes the reading further from neutral.
senses.whyCN: 效果由感官读取，加强就是把读数推得离中性更远。

senses.title: To concentrate a signal or colour
senses.definition: to increase the concentration of light, sound or colour in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 提高某一区域内光、声或颜色的浓度
senses.example: The filter intensified the red without changing the shape.
senses.exampleCN: 滤镜让红色更浓，却没有改变形状。
senses.why: Technical optics use the verb for concentration, the same tightening applied to a beam.
senses.whyCN: 技术光学用这个动词表示「集中」，即把同一股收紧作用用到光束上。

senses.title: To focus attention sharply
senses.definition: to make focus or concentration narrower and more forceful
senses.definitionCN: 使专注或集中更窄、更有力
senses.example: A deadline intensified her focus on the last chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 截止日期让她把注意力更集中在最后一章。
senses.why: A narrower beam is a stronger beam, which is why focus and intensity share a vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 光束越窄越强，所以「聚焦」与「强度」共用一套词。

intro.en: Intensify is formed in English from intense and the suffix -ify. Intense goes back to Latin intensus, stretched, the participle of intendere, to stretch toward.
intro.cn: 这个词在英语里由 intense 加后缀 -ify 构成；intense 可追溯到拉丁语 intensus「拉紧」，即 intendere「朝……伸展」的分词。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch, and it supplies intend, tend, tension and intense alike.
items.cn: 这个词意为「伸展」，供应了 intend、tend、tension 与 intense。

items.en: Intendere meant to stretch toward or direct attention to, with the prefix marking direction.
items.cn: 这个词意为朝某处伸展或把注意力指向某处，前缀标出方向。

items.en: The participle meant stretched tight, and that physical tightness became the English sense of strong.
items.cn: 这个分词意为「拉得很紧」，而这种物理紧绷变成英语的「强烈」。

items.en: English adopted intense through French, using it for heat, colour, feeling and attention.
items.cn: 英语经法语引入 intense，用于热度、颜色、情绪与注意力。

items.en: The suffix comes from Latin facere, to make, so intensify literally means to make intense.
items.cn: 后缀出自拉丁语 facere「做」，所以这个词字面就是「使强烈」。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the eighteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain in the sources.
items.cn: 这个动词自十八世纪有记录，确切首见年代在各家资料中不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the tense stem or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of increase.
note.cn: 第一组与「intensify」共享「拉紧」词干或只是形近；第二组是与「增强」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the strength or force of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物强度或力度的名词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of making something stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 指加强这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning very strong or very serious.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指非常强烈或非常严肃的。

entries.definition: Purpose or determination, from the same stretching verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指意图或决心，同出「伸展」动词。

entries.definition: To plan or mean to do, literally to stretch toward.
entries.definitionCN: 指打算，字面是「朝……伸展」。

entries.definition: The state of being stretched, the physical source of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 指被拉紧的状态，是这一族词的物理源头。

entries.definition: To make stronger, the broad neutral verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指使更强，是宽泛中性的说法。

entries.definition: To raise the level of a feeling or effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指提高情绪或效果的强度。

entries.definition: To make larger or louder, especially a signal.
entries.definitionCN: 指放大或增强，尤指信号。

entries.definition: To become or make more intense, often of conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 指升级、加剧，多用于冲突。

entries.definition: To make a feeling or problem more profound.
entries.definitionCN: 指使情绪或问题更深。

entries.definition: To add to something, often making it worse.
entries.definitionCN: 指叠加，常使情况更糟。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the stretched-tight participle, the -ify suffix and the fixed objects that pair with the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「拉紧」的分词、-ify 后缀，以及与这个动词固定的宾语。

normal.en: The participle meant stretched tight, so intensify is to tighten the string further.
normal.cn: 分词意为「拉紧」，所以这个词就是把弦再绞紧一点。

normal.en: Intense, intensity, tension and intend all come from the same stretching verb.
normal.cn: intense、intensity、tension、intend 都出自同一个「伸展」动词。

normal.en: The -ify suffix means to make, so the verb means to make intense.
normal.cn: -ify 后缀意为「使」，所以动词就是「使强烈」。

normal.en: Pressure, efforts, competition and scrutiny are its most common objects.
normal.cn: 压力、努力、竞争、审视是它最常见的宾语。

normal.en: It takes -ies, -ied and -ying, and the y never doubles.
normal.cn: 第三人称、过去式、现在分词依次换词尾，词干的字母不双写。

abstract.en: Intensity is not more of the same thing; it is the same thing held tighter.
abstract.cn: 强度不是更多同样的东西，而是同样的东西被攥得更紧。

abstract.en: A beam made narrower is a beam made stronger, and that is the whole word.
abstract.cn: 光束变窄就是变强，这就是这个词的全部。

abstract.en: Pressure intensified is not pressure doubled; it is pressure that no longer leaves room to breathe.
abstract.cn: 压力加大不是压力翻倍，而是不再留出喘息的余地。

examples.en: The company intensified training after the second accident.
examples.cn: 第二次事故之后，公司加强了培训。

examples.en: Wind intensified through the afternoon and closed the ferry route.
examples.cn: 午后风力加大，渡轮航线因此关闭。

examples.en: The debate intensified as new evidence appeared.
examples.cn: 随着新证据出现，争论更加激烈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因坦西法伊」——风箱越推越快，火苗窜成白色：加强、加剧

root: 拉丁语 tendere「伸展」→ intendere「朝……伸展」→ intensus「拉紧的」→ 法语 intense；英语十八世纪以 intense + -ify 构成动词，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all tighten one tension: strength, conflict, feeling, effort, scrutiny, effect, signal and focus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在收紧同一股张力：力度、冲突、感受、努力、审视、效果、信号与专注。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bellows speed up and the flame turns from orange to a blinding white.
core.cn: 核心意象：风箱越推越快，火苗从橙红变成刺眼的白。

branches.en: THE FORCE RISES: an action or quality is turned up on its own dial.
branches.cn: 力量上升：某项行动或性质在自己的旋钮上被拧大。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE TIGHTENS: a dispute or a system of checks is pressed harder.
branches.cn: 压力收紧：争端或审查体系被压得更紧。

branches.en: THE FEELING SHARPENS: emotion becomes too vivid to ignore.
branches.cn: 感受变锐：情绪鲜明到无法忽视。

branches.en: THE EFFORT THICKENS: work is made more frequent and more concentrated.
branches.cn: 努力变密：工作变得更频繁、更集中。

branches.en: THE EFFECT CONCENTRATES: contrast, colour or focus is brought to a narrower, stronger beam.
branches.cn: 效果集中：对比、色彩或专注被收成一束更窄更强的光。

intro.en: Intensify joins a Latin participle to an English suffix, so its affixes are the pieces of that joining.
intro.cn: 这个词把一个拉丁分词接在一个英语后缀上，其词缀就是这次接合的两端。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies tendere, intendere and intensus; facere supplies the suffix, and every piece is well recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 tendere、intendere、intensus；facere 提供后缀，每个部件都有清楚记录。

items.example: The verb is the physical source of tension.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是「张力」的物理源头。
它在 intendere 中标出方向。

items.example: The participle became the English adjective intense.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成英语形容词 intense。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a verb of increase.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表示增强的动词。

items.example: It appears in words such as intensify and amplify.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 intensify、amplify 这类词里。

items.meaning: the one or the thing that acts

items.example: It appears in tension, the oldest family member.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 tension 这个最老的家族成员里。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「加强；加剧」
由该动词加表示施动者或工具的名词尾构成，义为「加强成分」
由同一拉丁词干加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「强度」
由同一词干加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「密集的」

definition_zh: 专制的；独裁的；独断专行的
definition_en: relating to a ruler or system with unlimited power; describing a person who decides alone and allows no disagreement
core_image: 所有决定都汇到一个人手里，旁人不许插话
scene: 新主管从不征求意见，凡事一人拍板。 His autocratic style drove two editors to resign.
sceneCN: 这里 autocratic 是「独断专行的」（第 2 个义项）；句意是他专断的作风逼走了两名编辑。

pos.zh: 形容词：专制的；独断的

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

derivatives.zh: 同族名词：独裁者；独断的人

senses.title: Of a system with unlimited power
senses.definition: relating to a government in which one person or group holds absolute power
senses.definitionCN: 与一人或一集团掌握绝对权力的政体有关的
senses.example: The country had an autocratic constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家有一部专制的宪法。
senses.why: Auto- means self and kratos means power, so the word literally describes power held by oneself alone.
senses.whyCN: auto- 意为「自己」，kratos 意为「权力」，所以这个词字面就是「权力只归自己」。

senses.title: Of a person who decides alone
senses.definition: describing a person who makes decisions alone and tolerates no disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 形容独自作决定、不容异议的人
senses.example: Her autocratic manner annoyed the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她独断的作风惹恼了整个团队。
senses.why: The political sense transfers to daily life: a boss or parent who rules like a monarch is autocratic.
senses.whyCN: 政治义转到日常：像君主一样发号施令的上司或家长就是独断的。

senses.title: Of a manner that brooks no reply
senses.definition: showing a tone or attitude that expects obedience without question
senses.definitionCN: 表现出要求无条件服从的语气或态度
senses.example: He gave the order in an autocratic tone.
senses.exampleCN: 他用专横的语气下了命令。
senses.why: From the person the word narrows to the way they speak: a voice that leaves no room for answer.
senses.whyCN: 词义从人缩小到说话方式：一种不留回应余地的语气。

senses.title: Of power concentrated at the top
senses.definition: describing an organization where authority is concentrated in very few hands
senses.definitionCN: 形容权力集中在极少数人手里的组织
senses.example: The firm runs on autocratic lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司按高度集权的方式运作。
senses.why: The idea of one ruler scales to a structure: decisions flow from the top with no debate below.
senses.whyCN: 「一个统治者」的想法放大到结构：决定自上而下，下面没有讨论。

senses.title: Of a household run by one will
senses.definition: describing a family or small group dominated by the will of one member
senses.definitionCN: 形容由一名成员的意志主导的家庭或小团体
senses.example: It was an autocratic household where children never spoke first.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个专断的家庭，孩子从不先开口。
senses.why: The smallest stage for one-person rule is the home, so the word reaches domestic life.
senses.whyCN: 一人统治最小的舞台是家庭，于是这个词也进入家庭生活。

intro.en: Autocratic is the adjective of autocrat: auto-, self, plus kratos, power, so it means ruling by oneself alone.
intro.cn: autocratic 是 autocrat 的形容词：auto-「自己」加 kratos「权力」，意思是「独自掌权」。

items.en: Greek kratos, power or strength, is generally traced to an Indo-European root for strength; the exact reconstructed shape is disputed.
items.cn: 希腊语 kratos「权力、力量」一般被认为出自表示「强壮」的原始印欧语词根，具体重构形式尚有争议。

items.en: Autos meant self, the same element in automatic and autobiography.
items.cn: autos 意为「自己」，与「自动的」「自传」中的成分相同。

items.en: Autokrates meant ruling by oneself, with full power, and autokrator named such a ruler.
items.cn: autokrates 意为「独自掌权、拥有全权」，autokrator 指这样的统治者。

items.en: Autokrator was a Greek title for commanders and emperors holding full authority.
items.cn: autokrator 是希腊语中授予握有全权的统帅与皇帝的称号。

items.en: English took autocrat in the eighteenth century, at first for tsars and absolute monarchs.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 autocrat，最初用于沙皇与绝对君主。

items.en: The adjective autocratic later described any domineering person, from railway directors to aunts.
items.cn: 形容词 autocratic 后来用于任何专横的人，从铁路董事到姑妈。

note.en: The look-alike group is the self-power family; the near-meaning group grades kinds of harsh, top-down rule.
note.cn: 形近组是「自己掌权」词族；近义组按严酷与自上而下的程度分级。

entries.definition: a ruler with unlimited power
entries.definitionCN: 独裁者；同族名词。

entries.definition: a system ruled by one person
entries.definitionCN: 专制政体；同族名词。

entries.definition: in a domineering manner
entries.definitionCN: 专断地；同族副词。

entries.definition: relating to rule by the people
entries.definitionCN: 民主的；同用 kratos 词根，前缀相反。

entries.definition: like a dictator, imposing decisions
entries.definitionCN: 独裁的；语气更重，常含贬斥。

entries.definition: demanding obedience to authority
entries.definitionCN: 威权的；强调服从与限制自由。

entries.definition: using power cruelly and without limit
entries.definitionCN: 专制的；强调滥用权力与残酷。

entries.definition: trying to control others in daily life
entries.definitionCN: 盛气凌人的；日常人际，而非政体。

normalIntro.en: Autocratic is auto- self plus kratos power plus -ic: power kept to oneself.
normalIntro.cn: autocratic 就是 auto-「自己」加 kratos「权力」加 -ic：权力只留给自己。

normal.en: Auto- means self, as in automatic.
normal.cn: auto- 意为「自己」，如自动的。

normal.en: The root kratos also appears in democracy.
normal.cn: 词根 kratos 也出现在民主一词中。

normal.en: The noun is autocrat, the system autocracy.
normal.cn: 名词是独裁者，政体是专制。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ally: autocratically.
normal.cn: 副词加 -ally：专断地。

normal.en: Democratic is the opposite prefix on the same root.
normal.cn: 民主的是同一词根换相反前缀。

abstract.en: Picture every arrow pointing to one chair.
abstract.cn: 想象所有箭头都指向一把椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where only one voice speaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一场只有一个声音的会议。

abstract.en: Picture a household where children never speak first.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子从不先开口的家庭。

examples.en: The autocratic ruler tolerated no opposition.
examples.cn: 这位专制统治者不容任何反对。

examples.en: She resented his autocratic management.
examples.cn: 她反感他独断的管理。

examples.en: The board rejected the autocratic proposal.
examples.cn: 董事会否决了那份专断的提案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：auto「自己」+ crat「权力」+ -ic「……的」——权力只归自己、旁人不容置喙，就是专制的、独断的。

root: 希腊语 autos「自己」+ kratos「权力」构成 autokrates「独自掌权」与 autokrator「全权统治者」，经英语 autocrat 派生出形容词 autocratic；同族有 autocracy 与 autocratically。

sensesIntro.en: Power kept to oneself describes a whole system, a domineering person, a brooking-no-reply tone, a top-heavy structure and a one-will household.
sensesIntro.cn: 「权力只归自己」可形容整个政体、独断的人、不容回应的语气、高度集权的结构与一人说了算的家庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every decision flowing into one pair of hands while others are barred from speaking
core.cn: 核心意象：所有决定都汇到一个人手里，旁人不许插话

branches.en: a state with absolute rule
branches.cn: 绝对统治的国家

branches.en: a boss who decides alone
branches.cn: 独自拍板的上司

branches.en: a tone brooking no reply
branches.cn: 不容回应的语气

branches.en: power concentrated at the top
branches.cn: 权力集中在顶层

branches.en: a household run by one will
branches.cn: 一人意志主导的家庭

intro.en: The prefix auto- and the root -crat- build the family; the ending -ic makes the adjective, -ally the adverb.
intro.cn: 前缀 auto- 与词根 -crat- 构成词族；词尾 -ic 造形容词，-ally 造副词。

latinIntro.en: The elements are Greek: autos, self, and kratos, power; the same kratos gives democracy and aristocracy.
latinIntro.cn: 这些成分属希腊语：autos「自己」与 kratos「权力」；同一 kratos 也产生民主与贵族政体。

definition_zh: 循环的；血液循环的；循环系统的
definition_en: relating to the circulation of blood through the body, or to the system of heart and vessels that carries it
core_image: 一颗心脏连着满身血管，血液沿着环路不断绕行
scene: 这里指「循环的」。 The circulatory system carries oxygen from the lungs to every tissue.
sceneCN: 这里 circulatory 指「循环系统的」（第 1 个义项：由心脏、血管与血液构成的整套循环结构）；句意：循环系统把氧气从肺运送到每一个组织。图中可辨识物件：心脏、动脉、静脉、毛细血管网。

pos.zh: 循环的；血液循环的；循环系统的

senses.title: Of the blood system
senses.titleCN: 循环系统的：心脏与血管组成的整体
senses.definition: belonging to the system of heart, blood and vessels that moves blood around the body
senses.definitionCN: 属于由心脏、血液与血管组成、把血液送往全身的系统
senses.example: The circulatory system carries oxygen from the lungs to every tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 循环系统把氧气从肺运送到每一个组织。
senses.why: Latin circulus 'small ring' gives the idea of moving around a closed loop; the adjective names that loop's machinery.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 circulus「小环」给出沿闭环运行的想法；这个形容词命名这套环路机制。

senses.title: Of blood movement
senses.titleCN: 血液循环的：血液在体内流动
senses.definition: connected with the movement of blood itself rather than with the organs
senses.definitionCN: 与血液本身的流动有关，而非与器官有关
senses.example: Cold hands show poor circulatory flow at the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 手发冷说明体表的血液循环不佳。
senses.why: The same adjective can describe the flow and the structures that produce it, a normal split in medical vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词既可描述流动，也可描述产生流动的结构，这是医学术语中的常见分工。

senses.title: Of circulatory organs
senses.titleCN: 循环器官的：心脏与血管
senses.definition: describes the organs of circulation, chiefly the heart and the blood vessels
senses.definitionCN: 形容循环的器官，主要是心脏与血管
senses.example: Circulatory organs develop early in the embryo.
senses.exampleCN: 循环器官在胚胎早期就已发育。
senses.why: Anatomy attaches the adjective to the parts once the system is defined.
senses.whyCN: 一旦系统被定义，解剖学就把这个形容词附着在部件上。

senses.title: Circulatory disease
senses.titleCN: 循环系统疾病：影响心脏与血管的病症
senses.definition: describes illness of the heart and vessels, including high blood pressure and heart failure
senses.definitionCN: 形容心脏与血管的疾病，包括高血压与心力衰竭
senses.example: Circulatory disease is a leading cause of death worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 循环系统疾病是世界范围内的主要死因之一。
senses.why: Epidemiology groups heart and vessel disorders under one adjective because they share risk factors and the same prevention.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学把心脏与血管的病症归在同一个形容词下，因为它们共享危险因素，也共享同一套预防手段。

senses.title: Circulatory failure
senses.titleCN: 循环衰竭：血液无法满足组织需要
senses.definition: a state in which blood flow is too weak to supply the body's tissues
senses.definitionCN: 血流过弱、无法供应身体组织的状态
senses.example: Circulatory failure after trauma requires urgent fluids.
senses.exampleCN: 创伤后的循环衰竭需要紧急补液。
senses.why: Failure is the point at which the loop can no longer supply the tissue, so the adjective marks the system's breakdown.
senses.whyCN: 衰竭是环路再也无法供应组织的那一点，因此这个形容词标记的是系统的崩溃。

senses.title: Of lymph and other fluids
senses.definition: broadly, relating to the movement of lymph or other body fluids, not only blood
senses.definitionCN: 广义上指淋巴或其他体液的流动，而非仅指血液
senses.example: Lymphatic vessels form a separate circulatory route.
senses.exampleCN: 淋巴管构成一条独立的循环路径。
senses.why: Physiology extended the adjective to the second circulation that returns tissue fluid to the blood.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把这个形容词扩展到第二条循环，即把组织液送回血液的系统。

senses.title: Of a closed loop
senses.titleCN: 环流的：沿闭合路径周而复始
senses.definition: describes any arrangement that moves material around a closed circuit
senses.definitionCN: 形容任何让物质沿闭合回路周而复始运动的安排
senses.example: The reactor uses a circulatory cooling loop.
senses.exampleCN: 该反应堆使用一套循环冷却回路。
senses.why: Engineering borrowed the ring image for pumps and pipes that recirculate a fluid.
senses.whyCN: 工程学借用「环」的意象，指让流体反复循环的泵与管道。

senses.title: The system as a noun
senses.definition: rarely, the circulatory system taken as a noun phrase shortened to 'the circulatory'
senses.definitionCN: 罕用，指把 circulatory system 简称为 the circulatory
senses.example: The drug acts mainly on the circulatory.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药主要作用于循环系统。
senses.why: English often shortens the name of a system to its adjective with 'the', as with the digestive and the lymphatic.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把系统名称简化为「the + 形容词」，如 the digestive、the lymphatic。

intro.en: Circulatory comes from Latin circulatorius, built on circulari 'to carry around', from circulus 'small ring', a diminutive of circus 'ring'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: circulatory 出自拉丁 circulatorius，由 circulari「环绕运送」构成，而 circulus「小环」是 circus「环」的指小形式。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Circus named a ring, especially the round arena for races. From it came circulus, a small ring or circle.
items.cn: circus 指环，尤其是举行赛跑的圆形竞技场。由它产生 circulus，即小环或圆圈。

items.en: Circulari meant 'to form a circle, to move round'. Classical Latin used it for things going around rather than for blood.
items.cn: circulari 意为「成环、绕行」。古典拉丁用它指事物绕圈，而非血液。

items.en: William Harvey's demonstration of the circulation of the blood in 1628 gave the ring image its medical centre; the word circulation was extended from there.
items.cn: 1628 年哈维证明血液循环，使「环」的意象获得医学核心；circulation 一词由此扩展。

items.en: English circulatory appears in the seventeenth century, first in medical writing about the movement of blood.
items.cn: 英语 circulatory 于 17 世纪出现，最早见于关于血液运动的医学写作。

items.en: Later physiology and engineering applied the adjective to lymphatic flow and to any closed loop of pumped fluid.
items.cn: 后来的生理学与工程学把这个形容词用于淋巴流动，也用于任何泵送流体的闭合回路。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper origin of Latin circus is disputed; any Indo-European form behind it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：英语最早书证年代存疑；拉丁 circus 的更深来源有争议，其背后的任何印欧形式都属重构。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for the blood system and its flow.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是「血液系统及其流动」的近义词。

entries.definition: The movement of blood or the flow of anything through a loop; the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指血液运动或任何事物沿环路的流动；形容词描述属于它的事物。

entries.definition: To move around a loop or to spread; it names the action, not a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 沿环路运动或传播；它命名动作，而非结构。

entries.definition: A pump or person that keeps something moving around; a countable noun.
entries.definitionCN: 让某物持续环流的泵或人；是可数名词。

entries.definition: Means 'round in shape' or 'going in a circle of reasoning'; it does not name the blood system.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「圆形的」或「循环论证的」，并不指血液系统。

entries.definition: Relating to blood vessels; circulatory also includes the heart and the blood itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与血管有关；circulatory 还包括心脏与血液本身。

entries.definition: Relating specifically to the heart and vessels, the core of the circulatory system.
entries.definitionCN: 专指心脏与血管，即循环系统的核心。

entries.definition: Relating to blood as a tissue; it does not by itself mean the pump-and-pipe system.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为组织的血液有关，本身并不指泵与管道的系统。

entries.definition: Relating to the pressures and flows of blood; it describes physics, not anatomy.
entries.definitionCN: 与血液的压力与流动有关，描述物理而非解剖。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: circulus 'small ring' + -atory: the machinery of a closed loop.
normal.cn: circulus「小环」+ -atory：闭合环路的机制。

normal.en: The family runs circulate, circulation, circulator and circular.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 circulate、circulation、circulator、circular。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: circulatory system, circulatory disease, circulatory failure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：循环系统、循环系统疾病、循环衰竭。

normal.en: Harvey's 1628 work on the circulation of blood fixed the medical image of the ring.
normal.cn: 哈维 1628 年关于血液循环的工作固定了「环」的医学意象。

normal.en: vascular names the pipes; cardiovascular names the pump and pipes together.
normal.cn: vascular 指管道，cardiovascular 指泵与管道一起。

abstract.en: Picture a racetrack whose lanes are blood vessels and whose start line is the heart.
abstract.cn: 想象一条跑道，跑道是血管，起跑线是心脏。

abstract.en: Picture a city ring road on which traffic never stops and never exits.
abstract.cn: 想象一条城市环路，车流从不停下也从不驶出。

abstract.en: Picture a pump in a basement sending water around a sealed loop of pipes.
abstract.cn: 想象地下室里一台泵，把水送进一圈密封管道。

examples.en: The circulatory system includes the heart, arteries, veins and capillaries.
examples.cn: 循环系统包括心脏、动脉、静脉与毛细血管。

examples.en: Shock is a circulatory problem before it is anything else.
examples.cn: 休克首先是一个循环问题。

examples.en: The reactor's circulatory loop is checked every month.
examples.cn: 反应堆的循环回路每月检查一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「circul 圈 + atory 的」——沿着圈不停转的 → circulatory 循环的

root: 拉丁 circus「环」→ circulus「小环」→ circulari「环绕」→ 拉丁 circulatorius → 英语 circulatory。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: blood runs around a closed ring, and that ring can be named as a system, as a flow, as organs, as a disease, as a failure, as a second fluid, or as any engineered loop.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：血液沿闭合的环运行，而这个环可被命名为系统、流动、器官、疾病、衰竭、第二种体液，或任何人工回路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: blood running around a closed ring whose pump is the heart.
core.cn: 核心意象：血液沿一个闭合的环运行，泵是心脏。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM AND ITS PARTS: the whole ring and the organs that make it run.
branches.cn: 系统与部件：整套环路以及让它运转的器官。

branches.en: FLOW AND LOOP: the movement itself, whether inside a body or inside an engine.
branches.cn: 流动与回路：运动本身，不论发生在身体里还是机器里。

branches.en: WHEN THE RING BREAKS: disease weakens it, and failure stops its supply.
branches.cn: 当环断裂：疾病削弱它，衰竭则让它停止供应。

branches.en: THE SECOND CIRCULATION: lymph returns tissue fluid by a parallel route.
branches.cn: 第二条循环：淋巴沿一条平行路径把组织液送回。

branches.en: SHORTENED NOUN: the system can be named by the adjective alone.
branches.cn: 名词化简称：整套系统可以只用形容词来指称。

intro.en: Circulatory is a Latin verb of going around plus the functional adjective suffix -ory: circulat- + -ory.
intro.cn: circulatory 是拉丁「环绕」动词加功能形容词后缀 -ory：circulat- + -ory。

latinIntro.en: Latin circulus 'small ring' gives circulare and circulatorius, hence English circulate, circulation, circulator, circulatory and circular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 circulus「小环」产生 circulare 与 circulatorius，因此有英语 circulate、circulation、circulator、circulatory、circular。

items.meaning: relating to movement around a loop
items.example: Circulatory support kept the patient alive.
items.exampleCN: 循环支持维持了病人的生命。

items.meaning: to move around a loop; to spread

items.example: Poor circulation makes the feet cold.

items.meaning: a pump or person that keeps fluid moving
items.meaningCN: 让流体持续循环的泵或人
items.example: The heater has a small circulator.
items.exampleCN: 这台取暖器有一个小循环泵。

items.example: A circular argument returns to its start.
The Latin word circulus means a little ring.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁词 circulus 意为小环。

items.example: The Roman circus was a racetrack.
items.exampleCN: 罗马的 circus 是一条赛马场。

items.meaning: the heart, vessels and blood taken together
items.meaningCN: 心脏、血管与血液的整体
items.example: The circulatory system is closed in vertebrates.
items.exampleCN: 脊椎动物的循环系统是闭合的。

definition_zh: 壁垒；堡垒；保障；支柱
definition_en: a defensive wall or rampart; a strong protection or supporter of something
core_image: 厚实的城垛挡在城门之外
scene: 敌军压境，市民连夜加固城垣。 A free press is a bulwark of democracy.
sceneCN: 这里 bulwark 是「保障、屏障」（第 3 个义项：抽象的守护力量）；句意是新闻自由是民主的堡垒。

pos.zh: 壁垒；堡垒；防波堤；保障
筑垒防护；保卫

derivatives.zh: 近义词，义为「壁垒，防御土墙」（法语同源成分）
同族词，由荷兰语同源词入法语，义为「林荫大道」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「筑有壁垒的」

senses.title: A defensive wall or rampart
senses.definition: a solid wall or earthwork built to defend a place
senses.definitionCN: 为守御而修筑的坚实墙体或土垒
senses.example: Stone bulwarks ringed the medieval town.
senses.exampleCN: 石砌壁垒环绕着中世纪城镇。
senses.why: The Dutch source means timber stockade: planks stood up as walls.
senses.whyCN: 荷兰语源词本指木栅，木板竖立即为墙。

senses.title: The raised side of a ship
senses.definition: the raised planking along the sides of a ship above deck
senses.definitionCN: 甲板两侧加高的船板
senses.example: Sailors leaned against the bulwarks watching the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 水手倚着舷墙观望风暴。
senses.why: Any raised defensive edge extends from city wall to ship's rail.
senses.whyCN: 一切加高的护边都由城墙延伸到船舷。

senses.title: A strong protection or supporter
senses.definition: a person, institution or principle that defends something valuable
senses.definitionCN: 捍卫某项珍贵事物的力量或机构
senses.example: Independent courts are a bulwark against tyranny.
senses.exampleCN: 独立的法院是抵御暴政的堡垒。
senses.why: The physical wall is lifted into the moral one: protection without masonry.
senses.whyCN: 石墙升华为道义之墙，无砖无瓦同样御敌，义项转入比喻。

intro.en: Bulwark came through German from Dutch boornwork, a timber rampart.
intro.cn: bulwark 经由德语源自荷兰语，本指木制壁垒。

items.en: a reconstructed root bol- meant tree trunk or plank.
items.cn: 重构词根 bol- 指树干或木板。

items.en: bolwerk meant a rampart of piled timber.
items.cn: 荷兰语 bolwerk 指以木材垒成的壁垒。

items.en: Bollwerk carried the same sense into continental usage.
items.cn: 德语 Bollwerk 沿用此义并传播开来。

items.en: bulwark entered English for fortifications, then ship railings.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪 bulwark 进入英语，先指工事，后指舷墙。

items.en: bulwark now names any strong defender, chiefly in political and moral writing.
items.cn: 如今 bulwark 泛指坚强的守护者，多见于政治与道德论述。

note.en: Bulwark keeps its plank-root cousins close and stands by the fortress lexicon.
note.cn: bulwark 与同出「木板」词根的词相邻，同属堡垒语汇。

entries.definition: a wide street, from the same Dutch rampart word
entries.definitionCN: 林荫大道，与 bulwark 同出荷兰语壁垒一词

entries.definition: more than one bulwark
entries.definitionCN: bulwark 的复数

entries.definition: a timber fortress
entries.definitionCN: 木堡，同含「木块」词根

entries.definition: a partition on a ship
entries.definitionCN: 舱壁，拼形相近且同属航海词，词源稍异

entries.definition: a broad defensive wall
entries.definitionCN: 壁垒，防御土墙

entries.definition: a projecting fortification; a stronghold
entries.definitionCN: 棱堡；堡垒，据点

entries.definition: a fortified place
entries.definitionCN: 要塞，堡垒

entries.definition: a fortress protecting a city

entries.definition: a well-defended place or base
entries.definitionCN: 据点，大本营

normalIntro.en: Board upon board, a Dutch rampart stands as your shield.
normalIntro.cn: 木板层层相叠，荷兰式的壁垒就是盾。

normal.en: The root bol- means plank; werk means work, so a plankwork.
normal.cn: 词根 bol- 即木板，werk 即工事，合为「木板工事」。

normal.en: Boulevard is its soft modern descendant: a rampart turned promenade.
normal.cn: boulevard 是它的后代：壁垒变成了林荫道。

normal.en: Ship bulwarks stop waves, not armies.
normal.cn: 船的舷墙挡的是浪，不是敌军。

normal.en: A bulwark against something is the set phrase.
normal.cn: a bulwark against something 是固定搭配。

normal.en: German Bollwerk is the twin spelling.
normal.cn: 德语 Bollwerk 是它的孪生拼法。

abstract.en: Feel a stone shoulder take the siege ram's blow.
abstract.cn: 感受石墙肩头替你扛下攻城锤。

abstract.en: See a sea wall break the gray wave.
abstract.cn: 看见防波堤截断灰色的巨浪。

abstract.en: Hear a judge's gavel guard the courtroom door.
abstract.cn: 听法官法槌守护法庭之门。

examples.en: The treaty was a bulwark against further invasions.
examples.cn: 这项条约是抵御进一步入侵的屏障。

examples.en: Grandmother was the bulwark of the whole family.
examples.cn: 祖母是全家人的靠山。

examples.en: Sailors repaired the storm-damaged bulwarks.
examples.cn: 水手们修补了被风暴损坏的舷墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「布尔沃克」——布尔人「沃克」（walk）巡逻的壁垒，一步不漏地守着城墙。

root: bulwark 源自荷兰语 bolwerk（木板垒成的壁垒），词根一般追溯至原始日耳曼语 bol-（树干、木板）加 werk（工事），经德语 Bollwerk 进入英语；同源词 boulevard（林荫大道）由「壁垒」转指「壁上漫步之道」。词源学家或注：bol- 另有「圆木」说，来源略存争议。

sensesIntro.en: Timber walls defend a town, rise along a ship's side, and finally stand as moral protection.
sensesIntro.cn: 木板墙守卫城镇，延至船舷，最终化作道义上的屏障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: piled timbers standing firm against the enemy.
core.cn: 核心意象：层层木料垒成的壁垒，岿然御敌。

branches.en: the bulwarks of an old city
branches.cn: 古城的壁垒

branches.en: a bulwark against invasion
branches.cn: 抵御入侵的屏障

branches.en: leaning on the bulwarks
branches.cn: 倚着船舷护栏

intro.en: Bulwark is a compound of material plus work: what the planks make.

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic; Latin offers only the later synonym rampart.

definition_zh: 洋盆；海盆；大洋盆地；（海底）沉积盆地；深海盆地；海洋管理单元
definition_en: a large bowl-shaped depression in the ocean floor, together with the seawater and sediment it holds
core_image: 海底一只巨大的浅碗，碗壁是大陆坡，碗底铺着细软的沉积物
scene: 海洋学家在考察船上盯着声呐屏幕，海底的轮廓像一只巨大的浅碗。 The survey mapped a vast ocean basin beneath the Pacific.
sceneCN: 这里指「海底的大型凹陷单元」（第 1 个义项：海底地壳下凹、被海水与沉积物填充的巨大盆地）；句意为勘测船在太平洋海底测绘出一片辽阔的洋盆。场景物件：声呐屏幕、海底剖面线、大陆坡、沉积物。

pos.zh: 洋盆；海盆；大洋盆地（可数；复数 ocean basins）

collocations.phrase: the formation of an ocean basin

senses.title: Depression in the sea floor
senses.definition: a broad, bowl-shaped depression in the ocean floor
senses.definitionCN: 海底宽阔、碗状的凹陷
senses.example: The survey mapped a vast ocean basin beneath the Pacific.
senses.exampleCN: 勘测船在太平洋海底测绘出一片辽阔的洋盆。
senses.why: A basin is a bowl, so when the word is applied to the sea floor it names the bowl itself, not the water inside it.
senses.whyCN: basin 本义是「盆」，用于海底时命名的就是这只盆，而不是盆里的水。

senses.title: One of the named major basins
senses.definition: one of the large named divisions of the world ocean, such as the Pacific or Atlantic basin
senses.definitionCN: 世界大洋中被命名的大分区，如太平洋洋盆或大西洋洋盆
senses.example: Each ocean basin has its own pattern of deep circulation.
senses.exampleCN: 每个洋盆都有各自的深层环流格局。
senses.why: Geographers needed countable units, so the term was fixed to the named bowls that partition the global ocean.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家需要可数的单元，于是这个词被固定到划分全球大洋的那些具名盆地上。

senses.title: The water held in the bowl
senses.definition: the volume of seawater held within such a depression, treated as a reservoir
senses.definitionCN: 这样一处凹陷中容纳的海水量，被视为一个储库
senses.example: Warming has changed the heat content of the whole ocean basin.
senses.exampleCN: 变暖改变了整个洋盆的热含量。
senses.why: In climate accounting the container and its contents are spoken of together, so the basin comes to mean the water it holds.
senses.whyCN: 在气候核算中，容器与内容常被合在一起说，于是洋盆也指它所盛的水。

senses.title: Sedimentary basin under the sea
senses.definition: a depression beneath the sea in which sediments accumulate over geological time
senses.definitionCN: 海底在漫长地质时间内堆积沉积物的凹陷
senses.example: Drilling reached ancient layers in the ocean basin.
senses.exampleCN: 钻探触及了洋盆中的古老地层。
senses.why: Geologists care about what fills the bowl, so the term shifted from the shape to the sediment body that records its history.
senses.whyCN: 地质学家关心盆里填了什么，于是词义从形状转向记录历史的沉积体。

senses.title: Tectonic basin opened by rifting
senses.definition: a basin formed where the sea floor spreads or a continental margin stretches
senses.definitionCN: 海底扩张或大陆边缘拉伸所形成的盆地
senses.example: The rift opened a new ocean basin between the continents.
senses.exampleCN: 裂谷在大陆之间打开了一个新的洋盆。
senses.why: Plate tectonics explained how the bowl came to exist, so the term gained a process meaning alongside its shape meaning.
senses.whyCN: 板块构造解释了这只盆如何产生，词义便在形状之外多了一层过程义。

senses.title: Deep-sea floor province
senses.definition: the abyssal part of the sea floor, away from trenches and continental shelves
senses.definitionCN: 海底中远离海沟与大陆架的深海部分
senses.example: Fine sediment covers much of the deep ocean basin.
senses.exampleCN: 细颗粒沉积物覆盖了深海盆地的大部分。
senses.why: Oceanographers divide the floor into provinces, and the flat abyssal plains are the basin proper.
senses.whyCN: 海洋学家把海底分成若干区域，平坦的深海平原正是「盆」的本体。

senses.title: Regional marine management unit
senses.definition: a large sea area treated as one unit for pollution control or fisheries policy
senses.definitionCN: 在污染控制或渔业政策中被当作一个单元的大片海域
senses.example: The treaty set catch limits for the entire ocean basin.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约对整个洋盆设定了捕捞上限。
senses.why: Governments manage water at the scale of the bowl, so a physical term became an administrative one.
senses.whyCN: 各国按盆的尺度管理水域，物理词便成了行政词。

senses.title: Figurative vast receptacle
senses.definition: any very large enclosing space that seems to gather things into itself
senses.definitionCN: 任何巨大、包围性的空间，仿佛把事物收拢其中
senses.example: The old library was an ocean basin of forgotten journals.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧图书馆像一只洋盆，收着被遗忘的期刊。
senses.why: Once a basin is felt as a container, it can name any broad hollow that collects, even one far from the sea.
senses.whyCN: 一旦盆被感觉为容器，它就能命名任何广阔的收拢之处，哪怕远离海洋。

intro.en: Ocean basin joins Greek ōkeanos, the stream believed to encircle the world, to Old French bacin 'bowl'. The phrase itself is a modern geological compound. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ocean basin 把希腊 ōkeanos「被认为环绕世界的大河」与古法语 bacin「盆」并置；整个短语是近代地质学的复合词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek ōkeanos named the great river thought to run around the inhabited world; the word's pre-Greek source is unknown and every older root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 希腊 ōkeanos 指被认为环绕有人居住世界的大河；该词在前希腊语中的来源不明，凡为其拟出的更早词根都是重构形式。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as oceanus and used it for the outer sea, the great body of water beyond the known lands.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊词作 oceanus，用来指外海，即已知陆地之外的巨大水域。

items.en: Bacin 'bowl' came from late Latin baccinum; a Gaulish source *bacca 'container' has been proposed, but it is a reconstructed form and not a demonstrated origin.
items.cn: bacin「盆」来自晚期拉丁 baccinum；有说法认为出自高卢语 *bacca「容器」，但这只是重构形式，并非已证实的来源。

items.en: English basin first meant a washing bowl, then any hollow vessel or hollow place, and geologists later extended it to layered rock depressions.
items.cn: 英语 basin 最初指洗脸盆，随后指任何中空器皿或凹地，地质学家后来把它扩展到成层的岩石凹陷。

items.en: Ocean basin became standard in nineteenth-century oceanography, after deep soundings showed that the sea floor is divided into broad bowls rather than one flat plain.
items.cn: 十九世纪海洋学测得海底并非一整块平原，而是分成若干宽阔的盆，ocean basin 由此成为标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Greek source of ōkeanos is unknown, the Gaulish *bacca is a reconstruction, and the exact first printed use of the full phrase is not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：ōkeanos 的前希腊语来源不明，高卢语 *bacca 属重构形式，完整短语最早的印刷记录也未确定。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root or easily swapped sea and bowl words; group two holds neighbouring sea-floor features that are often mistaken for a basin.
note.cn: 第一组是同根或容易被替换的海与盆相关词；第二组是常被误当作洋盆的邻近海底地貌。

entries.definition: The body of seawater itself; an ocean basin is the depression that holds it, so the two stand as container and contents.
entries.definitionCN: 指海水本身；ocean basin 指盛住它的凹陷，两者是容器与内容的关系。

entries.definition: Any bowl-shaped depression on land or under the sea; ocean basin narrows the general word to the marine case.
entries.definitionCN: 陆上或海底任何碗状凹陷；ocean basin 把这个通用词收窄到海洋情形。

entries.definition: An adjective describing ocean features; it modifies a noun and cannot itself name the depression.
entries.definitionCN: 描述海洋特征的形容词；它修饰名词，本身不能命名那处凹陷。

entries.definition: The scientific study of the ocean; the basin is what the science studies, not the science itself.
entries.definitionCN: 研究海洋的科学；洋盆是它研究的对象，而不是这门学科本身。

entries.definition: The surface of the sea bottom; a basin is one particular depression in that surface.
entries.definitionCN: 指海底的表面；洋盆是这一表面上的一处特定凹陷。

entries.definition: A broad flat area of the deep sea floor; it is the floor of a basin, not the whole bowl.
entries.definitionCN: 深海海底宽阔平坦的区域；它是盆底，而不是整只盆。

entries.definition: A long, narrow, very deep depression; a basin is broad and bowl-shaped, while a trench is a slot.
entries.definitionCN: 狭长而极深的凹陷；洋盆宽阔如碗，海沟则像一道窄槽。

entries.tag: land drainage another sense of bas
entries.definition: The land area draining into a river or sea; it uses basin in the drainage sense, not the sea-floor sense.
entries.definitionCN: 河流或海洋的集水陆地；它用的是 basin 的流域义，不是海底义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的语素、真实的同族词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Basin is a bowl, so an ocean basin is the sea's bowl.
normal.cn: basin 是盆，ocean basin 就是大海的那只盆。

normal.en: Ocean descends from Greek ōkeanos, the river thought to encircle the world.
normal.cn: ocean 出自希腊 ōkeanos，即被认为环绕世界的大河。

normal.en: Geologists read the basin as an archive of sediment layers.
normal.cn: 地质学家把洋盆读成一部沉积层档案。

normal.en: The named basins are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic and Southern.
normal.cn: 具名的洋盆包括太平洋、大西洋、印度洋、北冰洋与南大洋。

normal.en: A basin holds water, heat and sediment, so it is both container and record.
normal.cn: 洋盆盛着水、热与沉积物，因此既是容器也是记录。

abstract.en: Picture a huge stone bowl sunk into the sea floor, its rim the continental slope.
abstract.cn: 想象一只巨大的石盆沉在海底，盆沿就是大陆坡。

abstract.en: Picture a library whose shelves are layers of sediment laid down over ages.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，书架就是千百年来铺下的沉积层。

abstract.en: Picture a world map divided into five enormous bowls, each with its own weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被分成五只巨盆的世界地图，每只盆都有自己的天气。

examples.en: The Pacific is the deepest ocean basin on Earth.
examples.cn: 太平洋是地球上最深的洋盆。

examples.en: Sediment cores from the ocean basin revealed a long climate record.
examples.cn: 取自洋盆的沉积柱芯揭示了一段漫长的气候记录。

examples.en: Treaties now manage fisheries across the whole ocean basin.
examples.cn: 各项条约如今在整个洋盆范围内管理渔业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ocean（海洋）+ basin（盆）」——海里那只巨大的盆 → 洋盆、海盆

root: 希腊 ōkeanos「环绕世界的大河」（更深来源不确定）→ 拉丁 oceanus → 英语 ocean；古法语 bacin「盆」← 晚期拉丁 baccinum，高卢语 *bacca「容器」为重构假说 → basin。两词在十九世纪海洋学中合为 ocean basin。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bowl: it is a shape on the sea floor, a named division of the world ocean, the water inside, the sediment filling it, a tectonic opening, a deep-sea province, a management unit and finally any vast receptacle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一只「盆」展开：它是海底的形状、世界大洋的具名分区、盆中的水、填入的沉积、构造张开的凹陷、深海分区、管理单元，最后引申为任何巨大的容器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vast shallow bowl sunk into the sea floor, its rim the continental slope and its bottom lined with sediment.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只巨大的浅碗沉在海底，盆沿是大陆坡，盆底铺着沉积物。

branches.en: SEDIMENT RECORD: the same hollow that gives shape also stores layers, so a landform becomes an archive.
branches.cn: 沉积记录：给出形状的同一处凹陷也存下层层沉积，地貌因此成为档案。

branches.en: THE NAMED BOWLS: a handful of great basins carry proper names.
branches.cn: 具名洋盆：少数几个大盆各有专名。

branches.en: CONTAINER METAPHOR: once treated as a vessel, the basin can hold heat, water or even forgotten papers.
branches.cn: 容器比喻：一旦被当作器皿，洋盆就能盛住热量、海水，甚至被遗忘的纸张。

branches.en: PLATE TO FLOOR: rifting explains how the bowl opens, and the abyssal plain is its mature deep-sea expression.
branches.cn: 从板块到海底：裂谷说明盆如何张开，深海平原是它成熟的深海形态。

branches.en: THE GOVERNED AREA: the basin becomes the unit treaties and agencies work in.
branches.cn: 治理区域：洋盆成为条约与机构工作的单元。

intro.en: Ocean basin is a transparent two-word compound: a Greek-derived sea word plus a Romance-derived bowl word. Its parts teach more than its inflection does.
intro.cn: ocean basin 是一个透明的双词复合体：一个源自希腊语的海洋词，加一个源自罗曼语的盆字。它的构词部分比屈折变化更值得注意。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer supplies oceanus and baccinum, while the Greek layer supplies ōkeanos; no single Latin verb lies behind the whole phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层提供 oceanus 与 baccinum，希腊层提供 ōkeanos；整个短语背后并没有单一拉丁动词。

definition_zh: 脾气坏的；爱争吵的；难相处的
definition_en: bad-tempered, argumentative, and difficult to deal with
core_image: 一位抱着胳膊守在门廊里的老头，见谁都要呛上一句
scene: 社区会议上，前排的老人对每个提案都要哼一声、反驳一句。 The cantankerous landlord refused every repair request.
sceneCN: 这里 cantankerous 是「难相处的」（第 1 个义项：脾气坏、好抬杠）；句意是这位难缠的房东拒绝了所有维修请求。

pos.zh: 脾气坏的；爱抬杠的
（机器等）难以操纵的；不顺利的（罕用）

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「脾气坏地；好争吵地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「乖戾；难相处」

senses.title: Bad-tempered and argumentative
senses.definition: irritable and eager to disagree, quarreling over small things
senses.definitionCN: 易怒且动辄抬杠，为小事也要争个不停
senses.example: A cantankerous neighbor complained about the noise before the party began.
senses.exampleCN: 派对还没开始，一位爱找茬的邻居就投诉起了噪音。
senses.why: The core image is a person whose first response to anything is opposition.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一个人对任何事的第一反应都是对抗。

senses.title: Difficult to deal with or manage
senses.definition: requiring unreasonable patience because of stubborn obstruction or contrariness
senses.definitionCN: 因顽固作对而需要付出超常耐心才能应付
senses.example: The cantankerous negotiations dragged on for months.
senses.exampleCN: 这场针尖对麦芒的谈判拖了好几个月。
senses.why: A person or process that fights every step makes simple tasks feel like tug-of-war.
senses.whyCN: 每一步都要作对的人或事，会让简单任务变成拔河。

senses.title: Frequently malfunctioning, of a machine
senses.definition: unreliable or hard to operate because of frequent faults
senses.definitionCN: 因频繁故障而不可靠或难以操作
senses.example: The cantankerous printer jams every third page.
senses.exampleCN: 这台老出毛病的打印机每打三张就卡一次纸。
senses.why: Machines that resist every command are treated like stubborn people.
senses.whyCN: 对每个指令都要作对的机器，会被当作倔人来对待。

intro.en: Cantankerous arose in eighteenth-century English, most likely from contek, an old dialect word for strife, blended with rancorous; the exact blend is debated.
intro.cn: cantankerous 诞生于十八世纪英语，一般认为由古方言词 contek（纷争）与 rancorous（积怨的）混合而成；具体拼合方式尚有争议。

items.en: Middle English contek, discord or strife, appears in northern dialects; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 中古英语北方方言有 contek 一词，意为争执、纷争；其更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Rancorous, from Old French rancor, deep bitterness, was well established in English.
items.cn: 源自古法语 rancor 的 rancorous（积怨的）在英语中早已根深蒂固。

items.en: The blend cantankerous appears in the eighteenth century, fusing contek and rancorous; scholars generally accept the blend though not its details.
items.cn: 十八世纪出现混合词 cantankerous，融合 contek 与 rancorous；学界普遍认可其为混成词，但细节尚有讨论。

items.en: The word spread in nineteenth-century fiction and journalism as the colorful label for grumpy characters.
items.cn: 十九世纪的小说与报章把这个词当作刻画暴脾气角色的鲜活标签而推广开来。

items.en: It remains a literary-flavored word for quarrelsome people and temperamental machines.
items.cn: 如今它仍带着书卷气，用以形容好争吵的人与闹脾气的机器。

note.en: Cantankerous has few relatives, being a blend word, but many near neighbors on the grumpiness spectrum.
note.cn: cantankerous 是混成词，亲缘词很少，但在「暴躁谱系」上近邻众多。

entries.definition: Full of long-held bitterness; one of the two words fused into cantankerous.
entries.definitionCN: 积怨深重的，是拼成 cantankerous 的两个词之一。

entries.definition: Likely to cause or eager for argument; overlapping but from a contend root.
entries.definitionCN: 好争论的、易起争端的，语义重叠但出自 contend 词根。

entries.definition: Like an ulcer or spreading sore; similar shape, unrelated meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 溃疡般的、腐蚀性的，形近而义远。

entries.definition: The noun naming the bad temper itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指坏脾气的抽象名词。

entries.definition: Easily provoked to anger.
entries.definitionCN: 一点就着的，动辄发怒的。

entries.definition: Rude and bad-tempered in a silent, sullen way.
entries.definitionCN: 阴沉粗鲁的坏脾气，偏沉默愠怒型。

entries.definition: Gruff and irritable but often with a hidden warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 粗鲁急躁但外冷内热的。

entries.definition: Given to picking fights and arguments.
entries.definitionCN: 动辄寻衅争吵的。

entries.definition: Cheerful, friendly, and hard to provoke.
entries.definitionCN: 和蔼友善、不易被激怒的，是 cantankerous 的反义对照。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the blend origin and the porch-and-argument image.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「混成词源」与「门廊抬杠」画面的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Blend story: contek, strife, plus rancorous, bitter, poured into one word.
normal.cn: 混成典故：contek（纷争）加 rancorous（积怨）灌进同一个词里。

normal.en: Picture formula: cantankerous old man is the classic collocation in fiction.
normal.cn: 画面公式：cantankerous old man 是小说里的经典搭配。

normal.en: Sound bridge: the -ker- in the middle echoes cranky and churlish, the family of grumps.
normal.cn: 语音桥梁：词中 -ker- 与 cranky、churlish 相呼应，同属「怪脾气」家族。

normal.en: Register note: it is more literary than grouchy, saved for colorful characterization.
normal.cn: 语域提示：它比 grouchy 更书面，专用于出彩的人物刻画。

normal.en: Machine use: a cantankerous engine treats the machine as a sulky person.
normal.cn: 机器用法：a cantankerous engine 把机器当作闹别扭的人。

abstract.en: Arms crossed on a porch rail, ready to reject whatever walks up the path.
abstract.cn: 双臂抱在门廊栏杆上，随时准备否决走上小径的一切。

abstract.en: A door that only opens if you kick it in exactly the right spot.
abstract.cn: 一扇只有踹在特定位置才肯开的门。

abstract.en: An old engine coughing black smoke at anyone who dares turn the key.
abstract.cn: 一台老发动机，谁敢拧钥匙就朝谁喷黑烟。

examples.en: Even the cantankerous committee chair smiled at the news.
examples.cn: 连那位难缠的委员会主席听到消息都笑了。

examples.en: His cantankerous letters to the editor became a local legend.
examples.cn: 他写给编辑部的抬杠信成了当地一景。

examples.en: The cantankerous old tractor finally surrendered to the mechanic.
examples.cn: 那台倔脾气老爷拖拉机终于向修理工缴械。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「砍坦克惹死」——脾气坏得像开坦克一样横冲直撞，谁都敢砍、谁都敢惹，一惹就翻脸，正是难相处、爱吵架的人。

root: 十八世纪英语混成词，一般认为由中古英语北方方言 contek（纷争，来源不确定）与 rancorous（积怨的，出自古法语 rancor）拼合而成，词形或受 cankerous 影响。学者普遍认可混成说，但拼合细节与比例尚无定论。指脾气坏、好争吵之人，后亦用于常出故障的机器。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from quarrelsome people to intractable negotiations and temperamental machines.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从好争吵的人延伸到难以推进的谈判，再到闹脾气的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure planted on the porch, contradicting everything that approaches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个守在门廊上、对来者一律唱反调的身影。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the grump whose yes is a rare event.
branches.cn: 人：那个「好」字极难出口的坏脾气。

branches.en: THE TABLE: talks where every clause is contested.
branches.cn: 谈判桌：每一条款都要争到底的对话。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: machines punished with human adjectives.
branches.cn: 工坊：被人类形容词惩罚的机器。

branches.en: THE COST: others' patience as the tax on contrariness.
branches.cn: 代价：他人的耐心是对作对性格征收的税。

branches.en: THE SOFTENING: the same word allowed to show hidden charm in fiction.
branches.cn: 软化：在小说里，同一个词也能透出几分可爱。

intro.en: Cantankerous is a blend: the ending -ous from rancorous rides on a compressed form of contek, strife.
intro.cn: cantankerous 是混成词：取自 rancorous 的 -ous 词尾，压在 contek（纷争）的压缩形式之上。

latinIntro.en: No Latin family attaches here; the word is homegrown English blending, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁词族，属于英语本土混成，拉丁同源列表留空。
